Engine-agnostic mindmap rendering for TiddlyWiki. Provides a canonical mindmap document model (MDOM), a per-view overlay layer for layout and restructuring that does not write back to wiki data, and a pluggable adapter contract for visualization libraries.

## Key features

- **Engine-agnostic** — pluggable adapters via `module-type: mindmapengine`. Ships with no built-in engine; install a companion plugin such as `rimir/mindmap-elixir` to render.
- **Three producer mechanisms** — `module-type: mindmap-producer` modules, JSON MDOM tiddlers, or a `filter=` quick form. All feed the same canonical document.
- **Base + overlay model** — view-specific positioning, hides, reparenting and custom nodes ride in a separate overlay tiddler (ordered op log). Multiple views over the same base data are first-class.
- **Structural editing (write-back)** — producers that declare `capabilities.structural` translate drag-rename / drag-reparent / addNode / removeNode into real wiki mutations (`renameTiddler` cascades references via flibbles/relink; `addTiddler`/`deleteTiddler` for create/destroy). Cascade-confirm modal guards large operations. Focus mode drills into subtrees.
- **Stable IDs with rename rescue** — producers assign deterministic IDs; orphaned overlay ops survive upstream renames and surface a manual prune action rather than silently disappearing.
- **Forward-compatible with slide mode** — the overlay op vocabulary doubles as the slide-ops vocabulary for the planned presentation player.

## Prerequisites

- TiddlyWiki 5.3.0+
- At least one installed engine plugin (e.g. `$:/plugins/rimir/mindmap-elixir`).

## Quick start

1. Install this plugin alongside an engine plugin.
2. Create a view tiddler with fields `mm.producer`, `mm.args`, `mm.engine`, `mm.overlay`.
3. Render with `<$mindmap view="MyView"/>`.

For a one-off mindmap of any filter:

```
<$mindmap filter="[tag[Knowledge]]" engine="MindElixir" overlay="MyMap/overlay"/>
```

## Architecture

See `doc/architecture.tid` (renders in the documentation tab when `doc-template` is installed) or the inline source comments in `widget.js`, `compose.js`, and `overlay-store.js`.

|!Version |!Date |!Changes |
|v0.2.21 |2026-05-17 |''Fix: post-create select races the refresh cycle.'' v0.2.20's create-and-select path called `engine.focus(newNodeId)` synchronously after `wiki.addTiddler` — but TW enqueues addTiddler change events for nextTick. So `focus` fired before the widget's refresh had reproduced + `engine.update`-d the new node into the canvas → silent no-op in the engine → original selection stayed visually highlighted; the widget's internal `selectedNodeId` was correct so the preview showed the new tiddler, but clicking the original node in the canvas wouldn't re-emit a select event (engines suppress no-change re-selects) → user had to click elsewhere then back to recover. v0.2.21 introduces a `createAndSelect(target)` helper that defers `selectByTitle(target)` by `setTimeout(0)`. The browser timer queue is FIFO; `wiki.addTiddler` enqueues its change-dispatch via `$tw.utils.nextTick` (also setTimeout(0) in the browser) BEFORE my deferred select, so the refresh runs first, the engine gets the new node, then focus + handleSelect fire correctly. `handlePreviewLinkClick` calls `createAndSelect` for both the in-subtree-missing and the self-prefix-fallback paths |
|v0.2.20 |2026-05-17 |''Self-prefix creation fallback for unresolved bare refs.'' When a user types `[[stock]]` inside a note at `private/knowledge/finance/investments/digital-coins` and no tiddler called `stock` exists anywhere, the namespace prettylink rule renders the link with `to="stock"` (the raw ref — walk-up didn't find a hit). v0.2.19 treated this as out-of-subtree and opened a browser tab to `#stock`, surprising the user who clearly meant "create a child of the current note". v0.2.20's `handlePreviewLinkClick` now interposes a `resolveAsCreationCandidate(target)` step between the `isInSubtree` check and the external-jump path: when (a) the widget has a current in-subtree selection AND (b) the ref isn't absolute (no leading `$`, no `://`) AND (c) `<currentTitle>/<ref>` lands inside the subtree, the click creates `<currentTitle>/<ref>` via `applyOps` addNode and selects it. The breadcrumb still pushes the FROM title so the user can pop back. Absolute paths the user typed in full (`[[private/knowledge/finance/foo]]`) continue to be handled by the existing in-subtree path; explicit out-of-subtree paths (`[[$:/SiteTitle]]`, `[[private/journal/…]]`) still fall through to external-jump map / new tab |
|v0.2.19 |2026-05-17 |''Preview-pane link navigation, breadcrumb, missing-tiddler create-on-click, external-jump mapping.'' Widget now intercepts `tm-navigate` events bubbling from inside the preview pane (`handlePreviewLinkClick`). Three outcomes: (1) ''in-subtree existing tiddler'' → pushes the current selection title onto a link-history breadcrumb at `$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<key>/breadcrumb-history`, then `selectByTitle` (a new shared helper extracted from `handleSelectNodeByTitle` — also used by the breadcrumb-jump handler and missing-create flow). (2) ''in-subtree missing tiddler'' → dispatches an `addNode` op through the producer's `applyOps` so the new tiddler gets the proper `kn.type` via `chooseNewNodeType`, then selects. (3) ''out-of-subtree'' → consults tagged-config mappings (`$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/external-jump` with fields `title-prefix` / `target-label` / `target-actions` / optional `target-view`); longest-prefix wins; matched mapping triggers a new modal at `templates/external-jump-modal` (Follow / Open in new tab / Cancel), no match falls through to the appify permalink workaround (`window.open(pathname + '#' + encoded, '_blank')`). Breadcrumb ''resets'' on canvas-originated selection (wired into the engine's `on("select", …)` callback in `initEngine`); pushes only on link clicks. The modebar restructured from a single horizontal row into a vertical container — top: wikitext-mounted breadcrumb (live-refresh on state-tiddler change via `forwardPreviewRefresh`), bottom: existing `.rr-mindmap-preview-modebar-row` with title + ✎ edit btn + select + ▶ play btn. New widget messages: `rr-mindmap-breadcrumb-jump` (truncate + select), `rr-mindmap-open-in-new-tab` (JS bridge for wikitext callers inside the widget tree). External-jump "Open in new tab" path uses a per-widget state-tiddler bridge (`$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<key>/open-in-new-tab`, consumed in the widget's `refresh()` hook) because the modal is rendered as a sibling of `<$mindmap>` so widget messages don't bubble back. Also new: `pending-select` state tiddler at `$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<viewTitle>/pending-select` — consumed once on engine init (`consumePendingSelect`) to auto-select a node after a "Follow" jump from another mindmap. CSS additions: `.rr-mindmap-preview-breadcrumb` + items / sep, `.rr-mindmap-extjump-overlay` + `.rr-mindmap-extjump-modal` mirroring the cascade-confirm-modal shell |
|v0.2.18 |2026-05-16 |New ''✎ edit'' button in the preview-pane modebar next to the title. Visible only when a tiddler-backed node is selected AND inspect mode is "body"; clicks set `$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<key>/preview-edit-state` to `yes`, flipping the wikitext branch to the `rr-text-editor`. Fixes the dead-end where empty-body nodes had no entry into edit mode (the default `rr-text-view-editable` template's double-click affordance only fires on existing text). Unintrusive styling — transparent background, no border, 0.45 opacity → 1.0 on hover. New `updateModebarEditButton` is called from `updateModebarTitle` and `updateModebarSelectedValue`, so the button reacts to both selection changes and inspect-mode changes |
|v0.2.17 |2026-05-16 |`knowledge-tree` producer gains two backward-compatible args. (1) ''`area-tag`'' (default `$:/tags/rimir/knowledge-app/area`) — the tag used to discover area tiddlers; override to host a parallel set of areas (e.g. priv-app's `$:/tags/rimir/priv-app/knowledge-area`) without polluting the public knowledge-app area list. (2) ''`root-prefix`'' (default `knowledge`) — the title-path root above the area id; multi-segment values like `private/knowledge` are split on `delimiter` so trees can live under any namespace prefix (e.g. `private/knowledge/finance/…`). Threaded through `produce()` (single-area + forest mode), `rootTitle()` (step-out depth), and `refreshFilter()` (refresh watch). `applyOps` (rename/reparent/addNode/removeNode) needs no changes — those operate on full titles inherited from the existing structural shape. The previous `AREA_TAG` module constant is now `DEFAULT_AREA_TAG`; behaviour is byte-identical for any call site that doesn't pass the new args |
|v0.2.16 |2026-05-14 |Docs + regression-test pin for the chain `mm.leaf-filter` source-iterator gotcha. Each chain leaf-filter is evaluated per-leaf with the leaf supplied via the producer's source iterator (`wiki.makeTiddlerIterator([leaf])`) — NOT bound as `<currentTiddler>` on the widget. Leading a run with `<currentTiddler>` therefore resolves to the //surrounding widget's// currentTiddler (typically a view tiddler title in appify usage), causing the run to silently reject every probe. `doc/reference.tid` gains an inline gotcha note on the `mm.leaf-filter` row; `test-grouped-tree.js` gains two paired regression specs: (a) implicit source `[get[rrt.type]match[meeting]]` keeps the chain populated (control), (b) the anti-pattern `[<currentTiddler>get[rrt.type]match[meeting]]` produces an empty chain (pinning the trap). Widget-scope vars like `<entity>` //do// resolve correctly because the widget IS the filter's variable scope — only `<currentTiddler>` is the trap |
|v0.2.15 |2026-05-14 |New chain-level opt-in field `mm.chain-hide-when-empty: yes` on the grouped-tree producer. When the chain's filtered leaf set is empty AND it has no rendering child sub-chains, the chain is omitted from the producer's MDOM entirely (no empty "(0)" bucket painted on entities the chain doesn't apply to). Default off, so all existing wikis remain byte-identical. The single-chain root-collapse branch was tightened to require exactly one surviving chain node so a multi-chain template that collapses to one isn't misrouted. 4 new specs in `test-grouped-tree.js` cover the opt-out default (empty chain renders), opt-in elision (empty chain dropped), opt-in non-empty (chain still renders), and the post-elision multi-chain root path |
|v0.2.14 |2026-05-14 |Flag-rule schema gains optional `mm.flag-tooltip` (text shown in the topic's native `title=` tooltip). Multiple matching rules stack their tooltips one per line in ascending-priority order. The decorator writes `mx:flag-tooltip`; the mind-elixir adapter's `_applyTooltips` combines it with any producer-emitted `core:tooltip` (core first, flags below) and stamps the result onto each `<me-tpc>`. Hovering a synthetic chain ancestor shows the aggregated flag tooltips too. 3 new specs (tooltip stamp, multi-rule stack, omission when no rule sets one). Companion `rimir/mindmap-elixir` 0.2.4 |
|v0.2.13 |2026-05-14 |''Filter-driven flag decoration''. New rule-tiddler schema (tagged `$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/flag`): `mm.flag-name`, `mm.flag-filter` (predicate filter over candidate leaf set), `mm.flag-aggregate` (`any`/`all`/leaf-only), `mm.flag-scope` (TW filter; `<<mm-producer>>` + `<<currentTiddler>>` visible), `mm.flag-priority`, plus visual primitives: `mm.flag-icon`, `mm.flag-text-color`, `mm.flag-bg-color`, `mm.flag-border-color`/`width`/`style`, `mm.flag-font-weight`, `mm.flag-font-style`, `mm.flag-text-transform`, `mm.flag-opacity`, `mm.flag-font-size-scale`, `mm.flag-class`. New pure-JS `lib/flag-decorate.js` (`loadFlagRules` + `decorateFlags`). Widget gains `flags=` attr / `mm.flags` field (filter resolves to rule titles). Decoration runs between produce and compose: inverted-loop evaluation (M filter calls, not N×M); bottom-up aggregation onto `core:synthetic` ancestors (`any` ≥1 leaf match, `all` 100%). Mind-elixir adapter translates `mx:text-color`/`mx:font-weight`/`mx:font-style`/`mx:text-transform`/`mx:opacity`/`mx:border` (→ `style.outline`, not `border`, to keep focus ring intact)/`mx:font-size-scale`/`mx:icons` (pipe-merged with `core:icon`) → inline `style.*`; stamps `data-mm-flags`/`data-mm-flag-classes`/`data-mm-synthetic` on `<me-tpc>`. Refresh-watch includes `[tag[$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/flag]]`. Stacking: rules sort ascending priority, style attrs last-wins, icons descending priority (most-important leftmost). 38 new specs (decorator leaf-level / aggregation / inverted-loop count / empty-tiddler skip / scope filtering / priority sort / invalid-value clamping; adapter mx:* → style.* translations; overlay setAttr override regression). Companion `rimir/mindmap-elixir` 0.2.3 ships the adapter side |
|v0.2.12 |2026-05-13 |''Chain-level leaf-sort'' for `grouped-tree`. New chain-tiddler field `mm.leaf-sort` — a TW filter applied to the chain's filtered leaves AFTER `mm.leaf-filter` and BEFORE the axis pipeline, so within each axis bucket leaves appear in the sort order (`groupBy` preserves first-seen). Examples: `[nsort[datetime]reverse[]]` (newest-first), `[has[due-date]nsort[due-date]] [!has[due-date]]` (most-urgent first, blanks last). Fail-safe semantics: empty result (typo / impossible predicate) keeps input order; titles outside the input set are dropped (a buggy filter can't smuggle in foreign tiddlers); input leaves the sort filter drops are appended in their input-relative order so no leaf vanishes silently. 7 new specs (no-sort baseline, asc/desc/reverse, multi-bucket cascade, blanks-last pattern, dropped-leaves append, empty-result fail-safe, foreign-titles ignored). 191/191 passing |
|v0.2.11 |2026-05-13 |New `grouped-tree` producer (Phase A read path) + four authoring-surface UX features. ''Producer'': declarative axis/chain/template schema for "flat entity set + multiple grouping axes" views (e.g. meetings grouped by year→month, then by state). Templates carry `mm.leaf-filter` (required), `mm.chains` (ordered list); chains carry `mm.axes` //or// `mm.sub-chains` (parent chain — renders each sub-chain as a synthetic child, parent's filtered leaves cascade); axes carry `mm.axis-field` or `mm.axis-derive` (filter) for group keys, `mm.axis-label-template` (literal mode or filter mode starting with `[`), `mm.axis-leaf-filter` (drop non-matching leaves at this depth), `mm.axis-sort` (`first-seen`/`asc`/`desc`/`enum` with `mm.axis-sort-keys`). Template options: `mm.initially-collapsed-axes` / `mm.initially-collapsed-chains` (id lists), `mm.show-counts` (appends `gt:leaf-count` attr — adapter forwards as `data-mm-leaf-count` so CSS can render `(N)` only while collapsed via `:has(> me-epd.minus)`). Stable id encoding: `gt:chain:<chainId>`, `gt:axis:<chainId>:<keyPath>` (cumulative pipe-joined key path so the same key under different ancestors yields distinct ids), `gt:leaf:<title>@<chainId>`. Empty-branch pruning drops groups whose recursive children are empty. Runtime axis-toggle state in `$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<canvas-id>/axes-disabled` (session-only). ''Four UX features'': (1) ''allow-node-creation'' — widget attr + view field `mm.allow-node-creation` (default `yes`). When `no`, engine adapter swallows Tab/Enter and context-menu "Add Child"/"Add Sibling" (mind-elixir blocks at keydown capture-phase AND vetos addChild/insertSibling/insertParent/finishEdit-of-placeholder ops, restoring canvas from cached MDOM). Engine-agnostic — adapters implement `setAllowNodeCreation(bool)`. (2) ''mm.root-label'' — view field overriding the producer's natural root label. Literal mode (any non-`[` string) or filter mode (starts with `[`, evaluated in widget's variable scope so parent `<$let>` vars like `<<entity>>` are visible). `grouped-tree` honours `args["root-label"]`; the other producers already did. (3) ''previewKindForId'' producer hook — classifies synthetic node ids into preview-kind descriptors (`{ kind: "chain"\|"axis", chainId, axisKey?, keyPath? }`). Widget writes the descriptor to `$:/state/.../preview-kind` and exposes `<<previewKind>>` / `<<previewKindAxisKey>>` / `<<previewKindKeyPath>>` to the `mm.preview-body-template` wikitext. Host templates branch on chainId to render kind-specific UI — e.g. orga-apps' preview-body transcludes the matching Notes/Tasks/Meetings view body so users get the same +new affordance and item list inside the mindmap pane. Only `kind === "chain"` opens the pane (axis kind reserved). (4) ''Saved view-state'' — two-layer overlay model. New view field `mm.overlay-filter` (TW filter resolved at execute() in widget scope; first result becomes overlay-target — use for per-entity persistence); falls back to legacy static `mm.overlay`. New `mm.saved-default` field — static tiddler title holding view-wide default ops. Compose merges saved-default ops (applied first) with live overlay (overrides — `setAttr` last-write-wins). New `overlay-store.peek()` exposes pending (debounce-buffered) ops so the toolbar buttons + composedOps see just-appended ops without waiting for the 250ms flush. Toolbar gains ''💾 Save as default'' (promote current overlay; disabled when overlay matches default) and ''🔄 Reset'' (clear per-entity overlay; disabled when empty). 183/183 passing (27 new specs: groupBy/applyChain/sortGroups, readers, multi-chain & sub-chain MDOM, id uniqueness across ancestor paths, axis sorting modes, filter-style label-template, initially-collapsed config, leaf counts, chain-level leaf-filter, allow-node-creation policy, root-label override, previewKindForId classification, mergeSavedAndOverlay precedence + end-to-end compose, overlay-store peek semantics) |
|v0.2.10 |2026-05-13 |Phase 3C-i — fullscreen player wiring. New filter operator `[<pres>mm-presentation-slides[]]` flat-maps a presentation's `mm.slides-order` to an ordered list of slide tiddler titles (one entry per node × that node's `mm.slide-order`). The `rimir/present` plugin (new soft dep) ships the actual `$present` widget; this release wires it up: a compact ▶ button next to the preview-pane modebar dropdown (visible only when the active presentation has at least one slide), a Shift+F2 hotkey scoped to the container (F5 / Shift+F5 are reserved by browsers; F2 alone is taken by edit-node), and a page-template tiddler `templates/present-overlay` that gates the `$present` overlay on `$:/state/rimir/mindmap/present-open`. New ''View'' toolbar toggle (gated on view-mode + structural producer) pins the preview pane open regardless of selection / inspect-mode — lets you reach the modebar dropdown to configure a presentation without first having to click an arbitrary node. ''Slides only'' button is now always right-aligned (was jumping left when title-mode warning was hidden). Shared `.rr-mindmap-toolbar-toggle` base style replaces the two duplicated button classes. Title-mode warning text rephrased — drag-reparent cascades references in every mode, only drag-rename is field-only outside title-mode |
|v0.2.9 |2026-05-13 |Slides-only follow-ups. (1) ''Pane visibility fix'' — `updatePreviewPaneVisibility` is now inspect-mode aware: Body / Slides require a selection; Presentation requires an active presentation. Previous logic (v0.2.6+) kept the pane open whenever a presentation was active on the view, blocking the canvas from reclaiming full width when deselecting in Body/Slides mode. To start a presentation from a clean canvas, click any node first → modebar appears → pick the presentation. (2) New container class `rr-mindmap-slides-only-active` on `<div.rr-mindmap>` — toggled in sync with the slides-only state so adapter / wiki CSS can target slide-bearing nodes selectively (e.g. only highlight them while pruning is active). (3) Architecture / settings doc notes added for the visibility rule and the container class hook |
|v0.2.8 |2026-05-12 |Slides-only view (Phase 3B). New canvas-toolbar toggle ''Slides only'' prunes the tree to nodes that have at least one slide OR have a descendant with slides — the presentation-eligible spine. Implementation: (1) `knowledge-tree` producer accepts new arg `slides-only=yes`; a bottom-up pruning pass drops branches whose entire subtree has zero slides, stamps `mm:has-slides=true` on nodes that own slides directly. Composes with focus mode (re-root first, then prune) and label-field (relabel first, then prune). (2) New producer-capability flag `capabilities.slides=true` — widget renders the toolbar button only when set. (3) Session state `$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<key>/slides-only` ($:/state/ so doesn't sync; transient view mode). (4) Pressed-state styling on the button (uses `<<colour primary>>` accent). 101/101 tests passing (5 new specs: no-op without arg, prune-empty-branches, keep-ancestors-of-slide-nodes, mm:has-slides stamping, root-preserved-when-empty) |
|v0.2.7 |2026-05-12 |Slides as tiddlers (Phase 3A). The single `slides` field is gone; each slide is now its own tiddler at `<owner>/slides/<slug>` carrying `kn.type=slide`, `tags=$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/slide`, `mm.slide-of=<owner>`, plus `caption`, `mm.slide-layout`, `mm.slide-notes`, and the slide body as the tiddler's `text` field. The owner's `mm.slide-order` TW list field drives display order. Wins: per-slide created/modified, tags, search, and rename-cascades-via-flibbles-relink-titles when the owner is renamed. New `lib/slide-tiddlers.js` (getSlideTitles / addSlide / removeSlide / moveSlide / freshSlideSlug / isSlideTiddler) replaces `lib/parse-slides.js`. Filter operators rewritten: `[<owner>mm-slides[]]`, `[<owner>mm-slide-count[]]`, `[<owner>mm-has-slides[]]` — input is now owner-titles, output is slide titles (the old field-text ops are gone). The `<$mm-slide-content>` widget is removed: slide bodies render via plain `<$transclude>` since each slide owns its text. The slide pane uses `<$edit-text>` against the slide tiddler's fields directly — every keystroke writes through, no buffer state. New slide via "+ Add slide" creates a blank tiddler and opens it in edit mode immediately (`rr-mindmap-add-slide` widget message). Knowledge-tree producer excludes slide-tagged tiddlers from both the tree enumeration and the refreshFilter — slides are content, not structure. 96/96 tests passing (21 new specs for slide-tiddlers, 7 rewritten for filters, 1 for produce-time exclusion, 3 for refreshFilter exclusion). No migration needed (no production data on the old model). Next phases: 3B slides-only view, 3C fullscreen player |
|v0.2.6 |2026-05-12 |Presentations — UX polish. (1) Unified the right-pane modebar dropdown: ''Body / Slides / <each presentation> / + New presentation…'' in a single picker (optgroup'd). Picking a presentation atomically activates it AND switches inspect-mode to "presentation"; "+ New" prompts, creates a `presentations/<slug>` tiddler, sets it active. The separate canvas-toolbar presentation selector was removed. (2) ''Click-to-select node titles'' — in Presentation mode, each member node title is now a button that dispatches `rr-mindmap-select-node-by-title`; the widget resolves it to a node id via the new `producer.idForTitle` (added to knowledge-tree) and calls `engine.focus()` to center+highlight the node on the canvas. (3) ''Visual slide cards'' — each slide in Presentation mode now has a header bar with "Slide N · <layout>", a coloured left border, and a subtle shadow so multiple slides on one node are visually separated. (4) Refresh efficiency — view-tiddler changes now only `refreshSelf` for actual structural switches (mm.producer / mm.engine / mm.overlay). Field tweaks like `mm.presentation` take a light-touch path: repopulate the modebar + update visibility, no engine reinit. Fixes the duplicate-canvas symptom that hit when "+ New presentation" caused refreshSelf to fire. (5) Preview pane is hidden again when there's no selection AND no active presentation — reverts the v0.2.5 always-visible behaviour. 107/107 tests passing (3 new specs for `idForTitle`) |
|v0.2.5 |2026-05-12 |Slides — Phase 2: named presentations. New tiddler convention (tagged `$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/presentation`, with fields `mm.view`, `mm.slides-order`, optional `mm.transition` / `mm.duration`) defines a playlist of nodes for sequenced playback. View tiddlers carry an `mm.presentation` field naming the currently-active presentation. New canvas-toolbar dropdown: ''[none] / <existing> / + New presentation…'' — picking writes `mm.presentation`; "+ New" prompts for a name, sanitises a slug under `presentations/`, uniquifies against existing tiddler titles, and sets the new presentation active. New actions-panel button toggles the selected node's membership in the active presentation's `mm.slides-order` list — label flips between "+ Add" and "−" based on current membership, hidden when no node is selected or no presentation is active. New `Presentation` option in the preview-pane modebar dropdown — switches the right pane to a sequence view that walks `mm.slides-order` and renders each member's `slides` field in order via `<$mm-slide-content>`. Preview pane is now always visible for view-mode widgets (was: hidden until a node was selected) so the modebar is reachable without selection — placeholder "(no selection)" appears in the title slot. New `[mm-presentations<viewTitle>]` filter operator returns presentation titles for a given view. 104/104 tests passing (5 new specs for the presentation filter). Phase 2 ships the read-side: authoring + playback list. Phase 3 will add presentation creation mode (visual fading of non-included nodes, per-slide overrides) and the fullscreen player |
|v0.2.4 |2026-05-12 |Slides — Phase 1. New `slides` field convention (wikitext slices separated by `===`, optional per-slide `!! layout:` and `!! notes:` directives) for storing zero-or-more slides per tiddler. A modebar atop the preview pane carries the selected tiddler title plus an inspect-mode dropdown ("Body" \| "Slides") — bound directly to a `$:/state/` tiddler via `<$select>`, so changes propagate reactively without JS-side bookkeeping. Slides mode shows a slide list with add/edit/move-up/move-down/delete controls per slide. New pure-JS `lib/parse-slides.js` (parse / serialize / update / insert / remove / move) — serialize emits a `!! layout: default` sentinel for empty default slides so inserts survive an immediate round-trip. New filter operators (`mm-slide-count`, `mm-slide-parse`, `mm-slide-get`, `mm-slide-update`, `mm-slide-insert`, `mm-slide-remove`, `mm-slide-move`); new `$mm-slide-content` widget for rendering slide text as wikitext (so cards live-render bullets, headings, etc. instead of showing source). Fix to `refresh()`: it now forwards to the preview-pane widget tree on every reproduce/recompose path, not just the fall-through — a slides-field write lands on a watched tiddler, and without the forward the right pane would only re-render after an unrelated change. 99/99 tests passing (26 specs for parse-slides, 17 for the filter operators). Phase 1 is foundation only — named presentations (Phase 2) and presentation creation mode (Phase 3) are not in this release |

Container + toolbar carry an `.rr-mindmap-title-active` class when a structural view is in title-label mode; CSS renders a soft red wash on the toolbar, a 3px red inset frame on the canvas, a 3px red top border on the toolbar, and reveals a bold red banner span "⚠ Title-mode — drag-rename rewrites tiddler titles and cascades references across the wiki." Preview pane explicitly keeps its neutral background. title: $:/plugins/rimir/mindmap/compose.js
type: application/javascript
module-type: library

Pure composer: applies an ordered overlay op log to a base MDOM and returns
the composite MDOM plus a list of orphaned ops (those whose target id is no
longer present in the base after upstream changes).

  compose(base, ops) -> { mdom, orphans }

The composer is intentionally side-effect free. It does NOT read or write
tiddlers; the widget calls it whenever base or overlay change.

Op vocabulary (see ./doc/reference.tid for the spec):

  { op: "hide",       id }
  { op: "rename",     id, label }
  { op: "setAttr",    id, key, value }       // value=null removes the key
  { op: "reparent",   id, newParent, index? }
  { op: "reorder",    parent, order }        // sparse; missing ids keep relative order
  { op: "addNode",    parent, node, index? }
  { op: "removeNode", id }

\*/

"use strict";

// Deep-clone a JSON-shaped MDOM. We don't use structuredClone because TW
// modules may be evaluated in environments without it (server-side jasmine).
function clone(value) {
    return JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value));
}

// Walk the tree and build an id->{node, parent, index} index. Mutating the
// returned `node` mutates the tree because we never clone here.
function indexTree(root) {
    var index = Object.create(null);
    function visit(node, parent) {
        if (!node || !node.id) { return; }
        var siblings = parent ? parent.children : null;
        index[node.id] = {
            node: node,
            parent: parent,
            index: siblings ? siblings.indexOf(node) : -1
        };
        var children = node.children || [];
        for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {
            visit(children[i], node);
        }
    }
    visit(root, null);
    return index;
}

// Detach a node from its parent. Returns the removed node or null.
function detach(entry) {
    if (!entry || !entry.parent) { return null; }
    var siblings = entry.parent.children;
    var idx = siblings.indexOf(entry.node);
    if (idx < 0) { return null; }
    siblings.splice(idx, 1);
    return entry.node;
}

// Insert `node` into `parent.children` at `index` (or append if index is
// missing/out-of-range).
function insertAt(parent, node, index) {
    parent.children = parent.children || [];
    if (typeof index !== "number" || index < 0 || index > parent.children.length) {
        parent.children.push(node);
    } else {
        parent.children.splice(index, 0, node);
    }
}

// Check whether `candidate` is a (transitive) descendant of `node` in the
// current tree. Used to prevent reparent cycles.
function isDescendant(node, candidate) {
    var children = node.children || [];
    for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {
        if (children[i] === candidate) { return true; }
        if (isDescendant(children[i], candidate)) { return true; }
    }
    return false;
}

function applyHide(index, op) {
    var entry = index[op.id];
    if (!entry) { return false; }
    entry.node.attrs = entry.node.attrs || {};
    entry.node.attrs["core:hidden"] = true;
    return true;
}

function applyRename(index, op) {
    var entry = index[op.id];
    if (!entry) { return false; }
    entry.node.label = String(op.label);
    return true;
}

function applySetAttr(index, op) {
    var entry = index[op.id];
    if (!entry) { return false; }
    entry.node.attrs = entry.node.attrs || {};
    if (op.value === null) {
        delete entry.node.attrs[op.key];
    } else {
        entry.node.attrs[op.key] = op.value;
    }
    return true;
}

function applyReparent(index, op) {
    var entry = index[op.id];
    var target = index[op.newParent];
    if (!entry || !target) { return false; }
    if (entry.node === target.node) { return false; }
    if (isDescendant(entry.node, target.node)) { return false; }
    detach(entry);
    insertAt(target.node, entry.node, op.index);
    return true;
}

function applyReorder(index, op) {
    var entry = index[op.parent];
    if (!entry) { return false; }
    var children = entry.node.children || [];
    if (children.length === 0) { return true; }
    var byId = Object.create(null);
    for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {
        if (children[i].id) { byId[children[i].id] = children[i]; }
    }
    var picked = [];
    var seen = Object.create(null);
    var orderArr = op.order || [];
    for (var j = 0; j < orderArr.length; j++) {
        var id = orderArr[j];
        if (byId[id] && !seen[id]) { picked.push(byId[id]); seen[id] = true; }
    }
    // Append any children not mentioned in `order`, preserving their relative order.
    for (var k = 0; k < children.length; k++) {
        if (children[k].id && !seen[children[k].id]) { picked.push(children[k]); }
    }
    entry.node.children = picked;
    return true;
}

function applyAddNode(index, op) {
    var parentEntry = index[op.parent];
    if (!parentEntry || !op.node || !op.node.id) { return false; }
    if (index[op.node.id]) { return false; } // id collision
    var node = clone(op.node);
    node.children = node.children || [];
    insertAt(parentEntry.node, node, op.index);
    // Update index incrementally so subsequent ops can reference it.
    index[node.id] = { node: node, parent: parentEntry.node, index: -1 };
    return true;
}

function applyRemoveNode(index, op) {
    var entry = index[op.id];
    if (!entry || !entry.parent) { return false; }
    // Recursively unregister descendants from the index.
    function unregister(n) {
        if (!n || !n.id) { return; }
        delete index[n.id];
        var children = n.children || [];
        for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) { unregister(children[i]); }
    }
    detach(entry);
    unregister(entry.node);
    return true;
}

var DISPATCH = {
    hide: applyHide,
    rename: applyRename,
    setAttr: applySetAttr,
    reparent: applyReparent,
    reorder: applyReorder,
    addNode: applyAddNode,
    removeNode: applyRemoveNode
};

/*
 * Public: compose(base, ops) → { mdom, orphans }
 *
 * base    : an MDOM document ({ version, root, crossLinks?, meta? })
 * ops     : an array of Op objects (may be empty or undefined)
 *
 * Returns a new MDOM (does not mutate the inputs) and the list of ops that
 * could not be applied because their target id was absent or invalid.
 * Orphans are reported with their original index so callers can offer a
 * "prune orphans" action without losing positional info.
 */
exports.compose = function(base, ops) {
    if (!base || !base.root) {
        return { mdom: base || null, orphans: [] };
    }
    var working = clone(base);
    var index = indexTree(working.root);
    var orphans = [];
    var safeOps = Array.isArray(ops) ? ops : [];
    for (var i = 0; i < safeOps.length; i++) {
        var op = safeOps[i];
        if (!op || !op.op) { continue; }
        var handler = DISPATCH[op.op];
        if (!handler) {
            orphans.push({ index: i, op: op, reason: "unknown-op" });
            continue;
        }
        var ok = false;
        try {
            ok = handler(index, op);
        } catch (e) {
            orphans.push({ index: i, op: op, reason: "exception", error: e && e.message });
            continue;
        }
        if (!ok) {
            orphans.push({ index: i, op: op, reason: "target-missing" });
        }
    }
    return { mdom: working, orphans: orphans };
};

// Exposed for tests
exports._internal = {
    clone: clone,
    indexTree: indexTree,
    isDescendant: isDescendant
};

<$fill $name="body">

!! Three collaborators

The `$mindmap` widget orchestrates three independent pieces. None of them know about the others:

|!Collaborator |!Module type |!Responsibility |
|Producer |`mindmap-producer` |Reads wiki data → emits base MDOM. Pure projection; never writes |
|Composer |`compose.js` library |Applies the overlay op log to base MDOM → composite MDOM. Pure function |
|Engine |`mindmapengine` |Renders the composite MDOM into the DOM. Emits user-gesture events back |

Plus the ''overlay store'' (`overlay-store.js`) — reads, writes (debounced) and appends to the overlay tiddler. Isolated so engine event handlers don't have to think about tiddler I/O.

!! MDOM (canonical document)

```
type MDOM = {
    version: 1,
    root: MNode,
    crossLinks?: { from, to, label?, kind?, attrs? }[],
    meta?: { producer, producedAt, source? }
};
type MNode = {
    id: string,           // stable, producer-assigned
    label: string,
    body?: string,
    children?: MNode[],   // tree by nesting; no parent field
    attrs?: { [k: string]: any }
};
```

Tree is by nesting. There is intentionally ''no parent field'' on nodes — that would create round-trip ambiguity when overlays reparent things.

!!! Attribute namespaces

`attrs` is the open extension point. Adapters MUST preserve unknown-namespace attrs across `update()`, so engine-specific overlay state survives engine swaps.

|!Prefix |!Owner |
|`core:*` |Engine-agnostic hints every adapter respects what it can (`core:icon`, `core:color`, `core:collapsed`, `core:hidden`, `core:tiddler`, `core:synthetic`) |
|`mx:*` |mind-elixir adapter (`mx:tags`, `mx:hyperLink`, `mx:expanded`) |
|`mm:*` |markmap adapter (future) |
|`kn:*` |knowledge-app producer (`kn:type`, `kn:tier`) |
|`tw:*` |TW round-trip metadata |

!! Base + overlay composition

The overlay is an ''ordered op log'' (JSON array in the overlay tiddler's text field), not a state snapshot. This is forward-compatible with v2 slide mode: a slide is just a named overlay (or a layered chain of overlays).

|!Op |!Effect |
|`hide` |Sets `attrs["core:hidden"] = true` on the target |
|`rename` |Replaces the target's label |
|`setAttr` |Writes / deletes a single attr key (`value: null` deletes) |
|`reparent` |Detaches and re-inserts the target under a different parent (with optional sibling index) |
|`reorder` |Sparse — sets the order of named children; un-named children keep their relative order |
|`addNode` |Inserts a new node under `parent`. The node id MUST be unique |
|`removeNode` |Detaches a node and discards it (distinct from `hide`) |

Ops whose target id is absent from the current base are returned in the composer's `orphans` array. The widget surfaces a count in its toolbar; the user prunes them manually rather than silently losing work after upstream renames.

!!! Two-layer overlay: saved default + live overlay

The compose pipeline accepts two op layers when the view configures them (v0.2.11+):

* ''Saved default'' (`mm.saved-default` field — static tiddler title). View-wide initial state. Applied first.
* ''Live overlay'' (`mm.overlay` static title OR `mm.overlay-filter` filter-resolved title). Per-render write-target. Applied second, overrides defaults — `setAttr` is last-write-wins.

`mm.overlay-filter` is the dynamic-per-entity pattern: the filter runs in the widget's variable scope, so a `<<entity>>` set by a parent `<$let>` becomes the per-entity overlay key. Empty filter result falls back to `mm.overlay`.

The toolbar exposes ''💾 Save as default'' (promote current live overlay to `mm.saved-default`) and ''🔄 Reset'' (clear the per-entity overlay → fall back to default → fall back to template's `mm.initially-collapsed-*`). Both buttons disable when their target operation is a no-op, reading `store.peek()` so just-appended (debounce-pending) ops count immediately.

''Gotcha for adapter authors:'' to make collapse/expand persist through the overlay, the adapter must translate engine-specific expand events into `setAttr core:collapsed` ops. In mind-elixir, that means listening to the top-level `bus.addListener("expandNode", ...)` event — it is //not// fired under the `operation` channel where structural ops live.

!! Structural editing (write-back to real tiddlers)

A producer can opt into ''write-back mode'' — turning the mindmap into an authoring surface for the underlying wiki, not just a display layer. The `knowledge-tree` producer is the canonical implementation.

!!! Producer interface

```
exports.capabilities = {
    structural: true,
    structuralOps: ["rename", "reparent", "addNode", "removeNode"]
};
exports.applyOps = function (ops, args, wiki) { ... }
exports.titleForOp = function (op) { ... }   // id → wiki title (for cascade counting)
exports.rootTitle = function (args) { ... }  // natural area-level root title (for step-out)
```

`structuralOps` is a whitelist — `setAttr`, `reorder`, `hide` stay visual-only even on structural producers, because collapse / sibling-order is canvas chrome that belongs in the per-view overlay.

!!! Per-op routing

`structural-ops.js → routeOp(op, producer, options) → { mode, count? }`. Modes:

|!Mode |!Caller does |
|`structural` |`producer.applyOps([op], args, wiki)` — mutates the wiki |
|`overlay` |`store.append(op)` — visual-only |
|`deferred` |Stash op in `$:/state/rimir/mindmap/pending-cascade`, pop confirm modal |
|`drop` |Silently discard (malformed op) |

The routing decision is per-op, not per-producer. Even on a `knowledge-tree` view, collapsing a branch goes overlay; only rename/reparent/addNode/removeNode mutate tiddlers.

!!! Cascade-confirm threshold

When an op would rename or delete more than `$:/config/rimir/mindmap/structural/cascade-threshold` (default 10) descendant tiddlers, `routeOp` returns `deferred`. The widget writes the pending op to a global state tiddler; a modal renders from it; on Confirm the widget bypasses the threshold check and applies directly.

Rename in label-field mode (see below) skips the cascade check entirely — only one field on one tiddler is touched.

!! Synthetic-node preview classification

Producers whose tree contains non-tiddler nodes (chain roots, axis groups in `grouped-tree`; future producers may have others) can implement `previewKindForId(id) → { kind, chainId, axisKey?, keyPath? } | null`. The widget calls this on every selection; for non-null returns it writes the descriptor to `$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<key>/preview-kind` (text = `chainId`; companion fields carry `kind`, `axis-key`, `key-path`).

The preview-body template tiddler (`mm.preview-body-template`) sees both signals:

* `<<previewTitle>>` — backing tiddler title for leaf selections (real-tiddler nodes).
* `<<previewKind>>` — chainId for chain selections (synthetic nodes). Empty for leaves.

The template branches on `<<previewKind>>` first to render kind-specific UI — e.g. orga-apps' preview-body transcludes `entity-notes` / `entity-tasks` / `entity-meetings` view bodies so the user gets the same +new affordance and list inside the mindmap pane. Leaves fall through to the per-tiddler detail block.

Only `kind === "chain"` selections currently open the pane. Axis-kind descriptors are still recorded for host templates that want to opt in.

!! Flag decoration pass

A fourth, optional pipeline stage sits between produce and compose: a ''flag decorator'' that walks the MDOM and stamps filter-driven visual attrs on tiddler-backed nodes.

''Why a separate pass?'' Producers project structure; engines render. Flags belong to neither — they're declarative visual rules a wiki author authors as plain tiddlers (`$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/flag`) without touching producer or engine code. By running between produce and compose, the decoration is producer-agnostic (any node carrying `core:tiddler` participates) and still overridable by overlay ops (a live `setAttr` lands after decoration and wins last-write).

''Pipeline insertion:''

```
produceBase()  →  decorateFlags(mdom, rules, wiki)  →  composer.compose(mdom, ops)
   producer            (new — flag-decorate.js)             compose.js
```

''Algorithm — leaf level:'' Collect every node carrying a non-empty `core:tiddler` into a title-keyed index. For each rule R, run `R.filter` ONCE with the index titles as the filter's source iterator. The result is the set of leaf titles that match R. Per-leaf decoration walks the index and stamps the union of every matching rule's contributions into the node's `attrs`. Net cost: M filter calls (one per rule), not N×M.

''Algorithm — aggregation:'' If any rule sets `mm.flag-aggregate`, a second bottom-up MDOM walk computes per-subtree (leaf-descendant count, matched-leaf count per aggregating rule), memoised once per node. Synthetic ancestors (`core:synthetic === true`) get stamped when the rule's policy (`any` / `all`) is satisfied. Non-synthetic ancestors are intentionally left untouched — a knowledge-tree parent doesn't pick up its child's flag without explicit author intent.

''Output attrs (engine-neutral):''

|!Attr |!Meaning |
|`mx:flags` |Space-separated names of matching rules (ascending priority order). Mind-elixir adapter mirrors to `data-mm-flags` on `<me-tpc>` |
|`mx:flag-<name>` |Boolean `true` per matching rule (finer CSS hooks) |
|`mx:flag-classes` |Space-separated `mm.flag-class` tokens (mirrored to `data-mm-flag-classes`) |
|`mx:icons` |Pipe-separated icon glyphs in DESCENDING priority order (highest-priority icon leftmost in the topic) |
|`mx:text-color`, `mx:font-weight`, `mx:font-style`, `mx:text-transform`, `mx:opacity`, `mx:font-size-scale` |First-class typography channels the adapter writes to inline `style.*` |
|`mx:border` |Composite `"<width> <style> <color>"`. Mind-elixir writes to `style.outline` (NOT `border`) to avoid clobbering the engine's focus ring |
|`core:color` |Background colour driven by `mm.flag-bg-color`. Reuses the existing channel so the adapter's auto-contrast foreground logic just works |

''Why `mx:*` instead of `core:*` for typography?'' These attrs are visual hints meaningful to engines that render text labels. A future graph-engine (e.g. a vis-network mindmap adapter) may not honour `font-weight`. Keeping them under `mx:` reflects "engine-specific intent" — a graph adapter can ignore them without surprise. Engine portability is at the //data layer//: a different mindmap engine adapter reads the same `mx:*` attrs and translates to its rendering model (cytoscape `data()` / `classes`, etc.).

''Refresh model:'' The widget watches `[tag[$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/flag]]`. Editing any rule tiddler triggers a `reloadFlagRules` + `reproduce` cycle. Deletion is also handled — the previous rule set's source titles are checked against the changed-tiddler set. No per-render caching in v1; the cost (M filter calls) is bounded and bounded sub-10ms in practice.

''Decorator → adapter contract:'' The decorator commits to the `mx:*` and `data-mm-*` shapes above. Engine adapters that want to participate read those keys and translate to engine-native style/data. The mindmap-elixir adapter does this in two places — `toMENode()` for the `style.*` channels and `_applyTooltips()` for the `data-mm-*` DOM attrs.

!! Allow-node-creation policy

Widget attr `allow-node-creation` (default `yes`) — with view field `mm.allow-node-creation` as fallback — controls whether the engine adapter responds to native node-creation gestures (Tab → child, Enter → sibling, context-menu "Add Child"/"Add Sibling"). When `no`, the widget calls `engine.setAllowNodeCreation(false)`; engine-agnostic — adapters that implement the hook block at the keydown capture-phase AND veto in-memory placeholder operations, restoring the canvas from cached MDOM. Used by views over //synthetic-structure producers// (grouped-tree, future tag-tree etc.) where a new node has no tiddler-of-origin to inherit from.

!! Focus mode

A view tiddler can declare `mm.focus` (or the widget can take `focus=`); the session-level override lives at `$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<key>/focus-title`. When set, the producer re-roots its MDOM at the focused subtree. The actions panel exposes ↓ focus-in / ↑ step-out-one / ⇪ step-out-fully buttons; step-out walks the focus title up one path segment and clears focus when it reaches the producer's natural `rootTitle()`.

The focus title is a structural identity (a tiddler title), so it survives renames via flibbles/relink — the producer reads it fresh on every produce.

!! Label-field configurability

By default each node's visible `label` is the leaf segment of the underlying tiddler's title. A view can set `mm.label-field` (or the session-state override `$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<key>/label-field`) to any other field — typically `caption` — to decouple display from structural identity. The actions panel includes a `<select>` populated from `$:/config/rimir/mindmap/label-fields` (default `title\ncaption`).

In non-title label-field mode:
* Producer relabels each tiddler-bearing node from the chosen field. Empty `caption` falls back to leaf segment (stamped `mm:label-derived="title"`); other empty fields render as `UNDEFINED` (stamped `mm:label-status="undefined"`).
* `applyOps.rename` writes the typed value to the chosen field — title is preserved, no cascade.
* `applyOps.addNode` derives the title slug from the sanitized typed value AND also stamps the typed (unsanitized) label on the chosen field of the new tiddler.
* `applyOps.reparent` still cascades structurally — only the //label// is decoupled.

!! Refresh model

The widget reacts to several signals:

# ''Base data change'' — `refreshFilter` (returned by the producer) is evaluated; if any changed tiddler is in the result, the producer re-projects.
# ''Overlay tiddler change'' — recompose from cached base, hand to `engine.update(mdom)`.
# ''Focus state change'' — reproduce (subtree re-root).
# ''Label-field state change'' — reproduce (new labels).
# ''View tiddler change'' — if `mm.producer` changed, the existing overlay is moved aside to `<overlay>/archive-<ts>` so stale ops can't leak into a new producer's MDOM; then `refreshSelf`.
# ''User gesture'' — engine emits an `Op` via `on("op", fn)`; widget routes via `routeOp` (structural / overlay / deferred).

The mind-elixir adapter advertises `capabilities.applyOps = false` — the widget always hands it a full composite MDOM via `update(mdom)` after a recompose. Per-op transitions in the adapter are a future optimisation.

!! Engine selection precedence

# Widget `engine=` attribute
# View tiddler `mm.engine` field
# `$:/config/rimir/mindmap/default-engine`
# First registered `mindmapengine` module (alphabetical iteration order)

!! Slide authoring — orthogonal fourth axis

Three things were orthogonal at v0.2.3 — structural source (producer), visible label (label-field), per-view overlay (collapse / reorder / hide ops). v0.2.4 introduced a fourth: ''per-node slide content''. v0.2.7 rewrote it from a single `slides` field into first-class slide tiddlers — the design constraints (per-slide timestamps, comments, search, rename-cascade) made the field model insufficient.

''Slide tiddler shape:''

|!Field |!Value |
|title |`<owner-title>/slides/<slug>` (e.g. `knowledge/llm/foo/slides/slide-1`) |
|`kn.type` |`slide` |
|tags |`$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/slide` (canonical marker; used by producer exclusion) |
|`mm.slide-of` |Owner tiddler title (back-reference; cascades on owner-rename via flibbles/relink-titles) |
|`mm.slide-layout` |`default` / `title` / `bullets` / any custom CSS class |
|`mm.slide-notes` |Single-line presenter notes |
|caption |Optional display name shown in the slide list |
|text |Slide body — plain wikitext, rendered via `<$transclude>` |

''Owner field:''

|!Field |!Value |
|`mm.slide-order` |TW list of slide tiddler titles in display / playback order |

''Why tiddlers, not a single `slides` field:''

* Each slide has its own `created` / `modified` — you can sort, search, audit per slide.
* Title-based identity → `flibbles/relink-titles` automatically renames the entire `<owner>/slides/<*>` subtree when the owner is renamed. The field model couldn't survive a rename of `knowledge/llm/foo`.
* Slide bodies become regular wikitext tiddlers — full search visibility, links cascade like any other tiddler, comments / tags / further fields can live on each slide independently.

''Producer exclusion:''

* The `knowledge-tree` producer's enumeration filter ends with `!tag[$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/slide]`, so slides never appear as nodes in the tree — only their owners do.
* The producer's `refreshFilter` also excludes slides, so editing a slide body doesn't trigger a wasteful tree-reproduce (the owner's `mm.slide-order` is what changes when slides are added/removed/moved, and the owner IS in the watched set).

''Pane composition:''

* The preview pane carries a modebar above its content. Vertical stack: (i) optional ''link-history breadcrumb row'' (wikitext-mounted, reading `$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<key>/breadcrumb-history`; hidden via `:empty` CSS when the stack is empty); (ii) horizontal row with the selected tiddler title on the left, a small ''✎'' edit button (visible only when a tiddler-backed node is selected //and// inspect-mode is `body`), then the unified dropdown on the right with `Body / Slides / <each presentation>  / + New presentation…`. Clicking ✎ writes `yes` to `$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<key>/preview-edit-state`, which flips the wikitext branch to render the `rr-text-editor` against the selected tiddler's `text` field. Provides a deterministic entry into edit mode for empty-body nodes (the default `rr-text-view-editable` template's double-click affordance needs existing text to surface).

!!! Preview-pane link navigation (v0.2.19+)

The widget intercepts `tm-navigate` events bubbling up from inside the preview pane (registered as `handlePreviewLinkClick`). Three outcomes:

# ''In-subtree, existing tiddler.'' Push the current selection's title onto the breadcrumb stack at `$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<key>/breadcrumb-history`, then call the shared `selectByTitle` helper (extracted from `handleSelectNodeByTitle` so the message-driven path, the link-click path, the breadcrumb-jump path, and the missing-create-then-select path all converge on the same engine-focus + handleSelect sequence).
# ''In-subtree, missing tiddler.'' Dispatch an `addNode` op through the producer's `applyOps` so the new tiddler gets the correct `kn.type` via `chooseNewNodeType` (same code path as Tab/Enter add-child). Sparse paths are fine — intermediate synthetic nodes don't need real tiddlers; `applyAddNode` only uses the parent path string for slug uniquification.
# ''Self-prefix fallback (v0.2.20+).'' If the namespace prettylink rule couldn't resolve the link (raw ref reaches `tm-navigate`) AND the current selection is in-subtree, the widget tries `<currentTitle>/<ref>` as a creation candidate. Catches the common case where the user types `[[stock]]` inside a note and means "create a child called stock" — without this, the click would hit the out-of-subtree branch and open a new browser tab. Skipped for absolute system-tiddler paths (`$:/…`) and obvious URL refs (`://`).
# ''Out-of-subtree.'' Consult tagged-config mappings (`$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/external-jump`). Longest-prefix wins. Match → write a `pending` state tiddler; the `templates/external-jump-modal` template reveal-mounts on it and offers Follow / Open in new tab / Cancel. No match → open the appify permalink directly (`window.open(pathname + "#" + encoded, "_blank")`).

The breadcrumb is a link-navigation //history stack//, not an ancestor path. Pushes only on link clicks; ''resets'' on any canvas-originated selection (wired by wrapping the engine's `on("select", …)` callback). The breadcrumb DOM is a small wikitext widget tree (`<$list>` reading the state tiddler) so any caption / title change propagates naturally via `forwardPreviewRefresh`.

Clicking a breadcrumb item dispatches `rr-mindmap-breadcrumb-jump` with a 1-based index; the handler truncates the history to `[0..index-1]` and calls `selectByTitle` — clicks are idempotent for cycles (e.g. A → B → A keeps the stack from growing).

''External-jump → Follow'' flow: the modal fires the mapping's `target-actions` wikitext (typically a sequence of `<$action-statewrap-set>` to switch appify channels) and, if the mapping has `target-view`, writes the clicked title to `$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<target-view>/pending-select`. The destination mindmap consumes this state once via `consumePendingSelect` (called after engine init) so the user lands on the linked node directly.

''External-jump → Open in new tab'' bridges back into the widget JS via a per-widget state tiddler (`$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<key>/open-in-new-tab`) because the modal is rendered as a sibling of `<$mindmap>` so widget messages can't bubble back through the widget tree. The widget's `refresh()` hook watches this state and calls `openInNewTab` + clears.
* Slide pane (`templates/slide-pane.tid`) walks `[<previewTitle>mm-slides[]]`, renders one card per slide. Edit mode is inline — each field uses `<$edit-text tiddler=<slide-title> field="...">` so keystrokes write through. No buffer state.
* `+ Add slide` dispatches the `rr-mindmap-add-slide` widget message; the widget creates a blank slide tiddler via `lib/slide-tiddlers.addSlide()` and writes the new title to `$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<key>/slide-editing` so the new slide opens in edit mode immediately.
* Up / Down / Delete in the slide card are pure wikitext: `<$action-listops>` on the owner's `mm.slide-order` (using the `move:N` / `-` operators), plus `<$action-deletetiddler>` for delete.

''Filter operators:''

* `[<owner>mm-slides[]]` — ordered slide titles.
* `[<owner>mm-slide-count[]]` — count.
* `[<owner>mm-has-slides[]]` — `yes` / `no`. Used by the slides-only view to prune nodes without slides.

!!! Slides-only view

A toolbar toggle hides every node that has no slides anywhere in its subtree. Implementation:

* Producer capability flag `capabilities.slides = true` — the widget only renders the toolbar button when the active producer advertises slides support (`knowledge-tree` is currently the only one).
* Session state: `$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<key>/slides-only` (`yes` / empty). $:/state/ means it doesn't sync — the choice is a transient view mode, not a durable preference.
* The widget merges `slides-only=yes` into `effectiveProducerArgs()` and watches the state tiddler in `refresh()`. A toggle triggers `reproduce()` — the producer re-runs and applies its pruning pass.
* Pruning is bottom-up: walk the tree, drop a node iff it has no slides AND no kept descendant. Synthetic root is always preserved (engine gets something to render even when no slides exist anywhere).
* Pruning stamps `mm:has-slides = true` on every node that owns slides directly — engines can style those distinctly (highlight, badge, ...).
* Composes with focus mode: focus re-roots first, then the prune trims the focused subtree. Composes with label-field: relabel runs before prune, so visible labels stay consistent regardless of mode.

''Refresh strategy:''

The producer's `refreshFilter` still excludes slide tiddlers (so a slide-body keystroke doesn't trigger a reproduce). The owner's `mm.slide-order` IS watched — adding or removing a slide via the slide pane writes to that field on the owner, which is in the watched set, which triggers a reproduce. The edge case "manually delete the slide tiddler without scrubbing `mm.slide-order`" leaves a stale visibility decision until the next reproduce — `getSlideTitles` filters out missing entries defensively so the canvas isn't broken, just stale.

!!! Named presentations

A presentation is a ''playlist'': a tiddler tagged `$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/presentation` with `mm.view` (the view it belongs to) and `mm.slides-order` (a TW list of member tiddler titles). The view's `mm.presentation` field names the currently-active presentation — durable, so the choice survives reloads.

* Decoupled from the per-view overlay. Presentations don't write through the overlay log; they're standalone tiddlers, which lets multiple presentations target the same view and lets the same node appear in multiple presentations.
* Storage: tiddler titles (not producer node-ids). Stable across producer swaps — only tiddler renames can break references (and Phase 3 will register the field with flibbles/relink for rename cascade).
* UI surfaces are colocated with the right pane (since "what does the right pane show?" is the question the dropdown answers): the preview-pane modebar dropdown unifies mode + presentation picking — options are Body / Slides / each presentation for the view / + New presentation… in an optgroup. The bottom-right actions panel gets a `+/−` toggle for selected-node membership in the active presentation. Clicking a node title in the playlist dispatches `rr-mindmap-select-node-by-title`; the widget resolves it via the producer's new `idForTitle` helper and calls `engine.focus()` to centre+select on the canvas.

Phase 3B (shipped in v0.2.8) added the ''slides-only view'' — the canvas can be pruned to nodes with at least one slide plus their ancestor spine. Phase 3C-i (shipped in v0.2.10) added the ''fullscreen player'' integration: a new filter operator `[<pres>mm-presentation-slides[]]` flattens a presentation to its ordered slide tiddlers, a Shift+F2 hotkey + compact ▶ button hand off to the `rimir/present` plugin's `$present` widget, and a page-template tiddler `templates/present-overlay` gates the overlay on a state tiddler. Phase 3C-ii (next) will add the ''presentation creation mode'' on the canvas — visual fading of non-included nodes, drag-to-reorder of `mm.slides-order`, per-slide overrides.

!! What this is NOT

* ''A graph engine.'' Use `flibbles/graph` + `cytoscape-engine` for general-purpose graphs.
* ''The slide player itself.'' This plugin produces the slide list and hands off to `rimir/present` for the actual fullscreen rendering — see [[its docs|$:/plugins/rimir/present/readme]] for navigation, layouts, and the deep-dive breadcrumb.

</$fill>
</$transclude>

<$fill $name="body">

!! Adding a new producer

# Decide the ''id namespace'' (e.g. `mp:` for "my producer"). All emitted node ids must use this prefix to avoid collisions with other producers.
# Create `producers/my-producer.js` + `.meta` (`module-type: mindmap-producer`).
# Implement `exports.produce(args, wiki)` — return MDOM with deterministic ids.
# (Optional) implement `exports.refreshFilter(args)` — TW filter expression; the widget re-projects when matching tiddlers change.
# Restart the server — `module-type` registration only happens at boot.

!! Adding a new engine adapter

# Create a separate plugin (e.g. `rimir/mindmap-mermaid`) — engine adapters do NOT belong in the core plugin.
# Bundle the library as `lib/foo.umd.js` (+ `.meta` with `module-type: library`).
# Stylesheet as a separate tiddler tagged `$:/tags/Stylesheet`.
# Implement `adapter.js` per `doc/reference` — must export `name`, `init`, `update`, `destroy`, `on`, `capabilities`.
# Set `capabilities.applyOps = false` for v1 — the widget will full-update on every change.

!! Map your engine's events to our Op vocabulary

When the user drags a node, your adapter receives a native event. Translate to:

```
{ op: "reparent", id: nodeId, newParent: parentId }
```

When a node is renamed:

```
{ op: "rename", id: nodeId, label: newLabel }
```

When the user collapses a branch:

```
{ op: "setAttr", id: nodeId, key: "core:collapsed", value: true }
```

Always emit via `this.on("op", op)` rather than mutating the MDOM directly. The widget owns the overlay; adapters do not.

!! Testing

* Use ''TestCaseWidget'' fixtures in `test/testcases.tid` for compose / producer round-trips.
* For engine adapters, prefer a stub adapter that captures `update()` calls to verify the widget's refresh routing.
* Manual browser tests cover real rendering — the test edition cannot exercise actual library behaviour.

!! Restart rules (rimir convention)

|!Change |!Restart? |
|JS module added/modified |Yes |
|Config tiddler edit |No |
|View tiddler edit |No (widget refresh handles it) |
|Overlay tiddler edit |No (widget recomposes) |
|Producer registration |Yes |
|Engine registration |Yes |

</$fill>
</$transclude>
"},"$:/plugins/rimir/mindmap/doc/examples":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/mindmap/doc/examples","created":"20260511000000000","modified":"20260511000000000","rdt.order":"4","rdt.plugin-key":"mindmap","rdt.plugin-name":"mindmap","rdt.plugin-subtitle":"Engine-agnostic mindmap rendering with base + overlay data model","rdt.section":"Examples","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"<$transclude $tiddler="$:/plugins/rimir/doc-template/templates/page">
<$fill $name="body">

!! 1. Quickest possible — any filter

```
<$mindmap filter="[tag[Knowledge]]" overlay="$:/state/rimir/mindmap/examples/quick/overlay"/>
```

The `filter=` quick form uses the built-in `filter-tree` producer with default settings: split each title on `/`, build the tree by common prefixes, attach tiddler text as node body.

!! 2. Knowledge-app — one area

Create a view tiddler `MyView` with these fields:

```
mm.producer:  knowledge-tree
mm.args:      {"area":"llm"}
mm.overlay:   $:/state/rimir/mindmap/views/llm/overlay
mm.engine:    MindElixir
```

Then anywhere:

```
<$mindmap view="MyView"/>
```

!! 3. Knowledge-app — all areas as a forest

```
mm.producer:  knowledge-tree
mm.args:      {"include-areas-root":"yes"}
mm.overlay:   $:/state/rimir/mindmap/views/all-knowledge/overlay
```

!! 4. Hand-authored MDOM

A JSON-typed tiddler `MyMap/data`:

```
{
  "version": 1,
  "root": {
    "id": "my:root", "label": "Core",
    "children": [
      { "id": "my:a", "label": "Branch A", "children": [
        { "id": "my:a1", "label": "Leaf A1" }
      ]},
      { "id": "my:b", "label": "Branch B" }
    ]
  }
}
```

View tiddler:

```
mm.producer:  json
mm.args:      {"tiddler":"MyMap/data"}
mm.overlay:   $:/state/rimir/mindmap/views/manual/overlay
```

!! 5. Multiple views over the same data

Create two view tiddlers pointing at the same producer/args but different overlays:

|!View |!`mm.overlay` |
|`MyView/personal` |`$:/state/rimir/mindmap/views/personal/overlay` |
|`MyView/team` |`$:/state/rimir/mindmap/views/team/overlay` |

Each persists its own positions, hides and reparenting independently.

!! Structural editing on knowledge-app data

The `knowledge-tree` producer turns the mindmap into an authoring surface over `rimir/knowledge-app`'s `knowledge/<area>/...` title tree. Create a view tiddler:

```
title: Mindmap/llm
mm.producer: knowledge-tree
mm.args: {"area": "llm"}
mm.engine: MindElixir
mm.overlay: Mindmap/llm/overlay
mm.label-field: caption
```

Then render with `<$mindmap view="Mindmap/llm"/>`. With `mm.label-field: caption`, drag-rename writes only the tiddler's `caption` field — titles stay stable, references stay intact. Without it, drag-rename rewrites the leaf-segment of the title and flibbles/relink-titles cascades.

The bottom-right floating panel offers:
* ↓ — focus into the selected node's subtree
* ↑ — step out one level
* ⇪ — step out fully to the area root
* ✎ — open the selected tiddler in a modal edit-popup (or F2)
* `<select>` — switch the visible-label field (title / caption / any field listed in `$:/config/rimir/mindmap/label-fields`)

Reparent a node with >10 descendants: a confirm modal asks before applying. Threshold is configurable.

!! Verification checklist

After installing both `rimir/mindmap` and a working engine adapter:

# Open a `$mindmap filter="..."/>` against a small known set of tiddlers; nodes match the expected count.
# Drag a node to a new parent in the canvas; reload the wiki; the node remains in the new position (overlay persisted).
# Rename a source tiddler in the wiki; the orphan badge appears in the widget toolbar showing the count.
# Switch `$:/config/rimir/mindmap/default-engine` between two installed engines; round-trip preserves `mx:*` attrs even when an unrelated engine renders in between.
# On a `knowledge-tree` view, drag-rename a node; verify the tiddler title changed (or — in label-field mode — that only the chosen field changed).
# Reparent a node whose subtree has more than `cascade-threshold` (default 10) descendants; verify the confirm modal appears with the correct count.

</$fill>
</$transclude>

<$fill $name="body">

!! Why not extend `flibbles/graph` instead?

The `flibbles/graph` widget uses declarative `<$node>`/`<$edge>` children — great for hand-authored graphs, awkward for "give me a mindmap of these tiddlers". Mindmap engines (mind-elixir, markmap, jsmind) take a recursive `{topic, children}` tree and expose tree-shaped runtime APIs (`addChild`, `expand`, `removeNode`). Tree-shaped contracts demand tree-shaped data and tree-shaped ops — a clean separation rather than re-shaping the graph model on every render.

!! Why an overlay instead of writing positions back to the source tiddler?

Three reasons:
* ''Multiple views over the same data'' — a single tiddler can appear in many mindmaps, each with its own layout.
* ''Derived structures that don't reflect the underlying domain'' — the user may want to group nodes for a presentation purpose without changing what the data "really" means in the wiki.
* ''Named presentations'' — a presentation is a separate tiddler with its own `mm.slides-order` referencing nodes from the view. Multiple presentations can target the same view independently of the overlay.

!! What happens if a tiddler is renamed?

The producer re-projects with the new title, so the old node id disappears from the base. Overlay ops targeting the old id become ''orphans'' — they remain in the overlay tiddler (your gestures are not silently destroyed) and the widget toolbar shows a count badge.

The badge is clickable: click it → confirm dialog → orphan ops are pruned from the overlay tiddler. You can also manually edit the overlay JSON or use the `mm.id-aliases` view field to map old id → new id.

!! Can a producer write back to TW data?

Yes — opt-in. A producer that declares `capabilities.structural: true` and a `structuralOps` whitelist takes mutation through its own `applyOps(ops, args, wiki)`. The widget routes each user-emitted op individually: rename/reparent/addNode/removeNode mutate wiki tiddlers; everything else (collapse, sibling order, custom attrs) still lives in the per-view overlay. The `knowledge-tree` producer is the canonical example — it translates drag-rename / drag-reparent into `wiki.renameTiddler` so flibbles/relink cascades references.

!! Will my drag-rename change my tiddler titles?

Depends on the visible-label mode. The actions panel has a small dropdown:
* ''title'' (default) — yes, rename rewrites the leaf segment of the tiddler title and cascades references via flibbles/relink-titles. The widget makes this mode visually obvious: a soft red wash on the toolbar, a 3px red frame around the canvas, and a bold banner in the toolbar reading "⚠ Title-mode — drag-rename rewrites tiddler titles and cascades references across the wiki."
* ''caption'' (or any other field) — no, rename only writes to the chosen field. Title is preserved, references untouched. The visual warning disappears.

This is the structural-vs-visual decoupling: keep titles as stable path-segment identities (good for backlinks, addressing, references) and put the human-friendly label in `caption` (or wherever you like).

!! Why not use `json-dsl` for producers?

`json-dsl` is a widget-based JSON builder (`<$json-obj>`, `<$json-prop>`, etc.) — useful for hand-authored JSON, but not a filter-to-tree compiler. Producers are JS modules so they can do the segmentation/walking efficiently, and so the engine adapter can call `producer.produce()` synchronously inside `init()` without rendering a widget tree.

!! What if my engine doesn't support a feature like cross-links?

Set `capabilities.applyOps = false` (or omit specific capabilities) and the widget falls back to engine-agnostic behaviour. Unknown attrs in the namespace bag are preserved on round-trip but not visualised — switching to a more capable engine reveals them without data loss.

!! What happens if I switch `mm.producer` on a view that already has overlay ops?

The widget detects the change before tearing down, archives the live overlay to `<overlay-title>/archive-<timestamp>` (preserving all fields, plus stamps `mm.archived-from-producer` and `mm.archived-at`), and clears the live overlay. The new producer starts fresh — its MDOM uses a different id encoding, so the old ops would silently no-op against it anyway. The archive is a regular tiddler you can inspect and copy ops back out of if needed.

!! Operation affected too many descendants — what's the threshold?

`$:/config/rimir/mindmap/structural/cascade-threshold`, default 10. Above that, rename / reparent / removeNode pops a confirm modal showing the count. Confirm applies the op via `applyOps`; Cancel discards. Set the threshold to a very high number to disable confirmation entirely.

Note: rename in label-field mode (caption etc.) skips the threshold check — it only writes one field on one tiddler.

!! Will there be a visual editor for view tiddlers?

Not in v1. Use the standard TW tiddler editor and set the `mm.*` fields by hand or via a small action button. A view designer is on the roadmap once the contract proves stable.

</$fill>
</$transclude>

<$fill $name="body">

!! What flag rules do

A ''flag rule'' is a tiddler tagged `$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/flag` that attaches a visual signal to every mindmap node matching a filter. Authoring a rule looks like this:

```
title: $:/my-flags/critical
tags: $:/tags/rimir/mindmap/flag
mm.flag-name: critical
mm.flag-filter: [priority[critical]]
mm.flag-icon: 🔥
mm.flag-font-weight: bold
mm.flag-aggregate: any
```

Whenever this rule is loaded by a mindmap view, every tiddler-backed leaf whose `priority` field is `critical` shows the 🔥 icon and a bold label. Synthetic chain/axis nodes whose subtree contains ≥1 critical leaf inherit the icon too (aggregation: `any`).

''Why not stamp icons directly on tiddlers?'' Two reasons:

* The same tiddler can fan out into many views (Tasks chain, Notes chain, …). One filter-driven rule is more correct than N hand-stamps.
* Conditions like //"overdue //and// not yet completed"// derive from multiple fields. Filter rules let the visual signal track field changes automatically.

!! Opting a view in

Per-view:

```
mm.flags: [tag[$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/flag]tag[orga-apps]]
```

Or per-widget (overrides the field):

```
<$mindmap view="..." flags="[tag[$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/flag]tag[orga-apps]]"/>
```

The empty default — no `mm.flags`, no `flags=` — is intentional: third-party plugins can ship rule tiddlers without affecting unrelated views.

!! Field reference

See //Reference > Flag decoration// for the full schema. The most common subset:

* `mm.flag-name` (required) — slug used in `data-mm-flags` and per-flag boolean attr.
* `mm.flag-filter` (required) — //predicate filter// applied to the candidate leaf set. Use `[priority[critical]]`, not `[is[current]priority[critical]]`.
* `mm.flag-icon` — single glyph; stacks with other matching rules' icons.
* `mm.flag-text-color`, `mm.flag-bg-color`, `mm.flag-border-color`/`width`/`style`, `mm.flag-font-weight`, `mm.flag-font-style`, `mm.flag-text-transform`, `mm.flag-opacity`, `mm.flag-font-size-scale` — typography & decoration.
* `mm.flag-aggregate` — `any` / `all` / empty (leaf-only).
* `mm.flag-priority` — integer; higher applied later (last-wins for style conflicts), icon appears further left.
* `mm.flag-scope` — TW filter restricting which views/producers the rule applies to. `<<mm-producer>>` and `<<currentTiddler>>` (= view title) are visible.
* `mm.flag-tooltip` — text shown in the native browser tooltip when the user hovers the topic. Multiple matching rules stack their tooltips (one line each).

!! Recipes

!!! Bold + red border for high priority

```
mm.flag-name: critical
mm.flag-filter: [priority[critical]] [priority[high]]
mm.flag-font-weight: bold
mm.flag-border-color: #d04444
mm.flag-border-width: 2px
mm.flag-border-style: solid
mm.flag-priority: 30
```

!!! Dimmed italic for archived items

```
mm.flag-name: archived
mm.flag-filter: [status[archived]]
mm.flag-opacity: 0.5
mm.flag-font-style: italic
mm.flag-priority: 5
```

!!! Aggregate parent badge: any descendant is overdue

```
mm.flag-name: overdue
mm.flag-filter: [!status[completed]oa-task-urgency[]match[Past]]
mm.flag-icon: ⏰
mm.flag-text-transform: uppercase
mm.flag-aggregate: any
```

The chain root that owns an overdue leaf now also shows ⏰ — useful as a tab badge.

!!! Scope a rule to one producer

```
mm.flag-scope: [<mm-producer>match[grouped-tree]]
```

The rule is loaded only when the view's producer is `grouped-tree`. Other views (knowledge-tree, json, filter-tree, …) see it as if it didn't exist.

!!! Multi-icon stack with priority ordering

Two rules matching the same task — `critical` (priority 30, icon 🔥) and `overdue` (priority 20, icon ⏰). The leaf renders 🔥 ⏰ — descending priority, so the most-important icon is leftmost. Style conflicts resolve last-wins (priority 30 overrides priority 20).

!!! Hover tooltips

Add `mm.flag-tooltip` to give the user a human-readable explanation when they hover the topic:

```
mm.flag-tooltip: ⏰ Overdue — past due-date, still open
```

If multiple rules match a node, each rule's tooltip becomes one line of the topic's native `title=` attribute (browser tooltip), ordered by ascending priority. If the producer also emits a `core:tooltip` (e.g. knowledge-tree's structural breadcrumb), that line comes first and the flag block follows below.

!! CSS hooks

For effects the schema doesn't cover directly, target the DOM attrs the mind-elixir adapter stamps:

```
me-tpc[data-mm-flags~="urgent"]::before {
    content: "!";
    color: #d04444;
    margin-right: 4px;
    font-weight: bold;
}

/* Tone aggregation down on synthetic ancestors */
me-tpc[data-mm-flags~="overdue"][data-mm-synthetic="yes"] {
    text-transform: none;
    outline: none;
}
```

`mm.flag-class` adds custom class tokens to `data-mm-flag-classes`:

```
mm.flag-class: kn-priority-bump
```

→ DOM: `<me-tpc data-mm-flag-classes="kn-priority-bump">`. Author the CSS in your own theme tiddler.

!! Gotchas

* ''Plugin-shipped rules are SHADOWS — the `mm.flags` filter must traverse shadows.'' Tiddlers shipped inside a plugin (e.g. `$:/plugins/foo/flags/bar`) are shadow tiddlers, and TW's bare `[tag[X]]` operator only sees //regular// tiddlers. Always start a discovery filter with `[all[tiddlers+shadows]tag[...]]` — otherwise you'll silently load zero rules. Example:
:`mm.flags: [all[tiddlers+shadows]tag[$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/flag]tag[orga-apps]]`
* ''Predicate filter form.'' The decorator passes candidate leaf titles as the filter's source iterator. Use plain field operators (`[priority[critical]]`); `[is[current]…]` won't match because `currentTiddler` isn't bound during the inverted-loop call.
* ''Preserve titles when the filter ends with a value-returning operator.'' Operators like `oa-task-urgency[]`, `get[…]`, `addsuffix[…]` //replace// each input title with a derived string, so the filter output becomes a list of strings — not the task titles the decorator needs. Use `:filter[…]` to keep titles while testing a predicate:
:`[rrt.type[task]!status[completed]] :filter[oa-task-urgency[]match[Past]]`
:The `:filter[X]` accumulator keeps each item where running X with that item as the source returns non-empty — and preserves the original title in the output.
* ''Outline, not border.'' Mind-elixir uses `border` on the topic bubble for its focus ring. The decorator's `mm.flag-border-*` composite is rendered to `style.outline` so the focus ring stays intact.
* ''Aggregation only stamps synthetic nodes.'' A tiddler-backed parent (knowledge-tree parent note) never inherits a child's flag — intentional, to avoid surprise styling on real tiddlers.
* ''Edits trigger refresh on every keystroke.'' The widget watches `[tag[$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/flag]]`. Editing a rule's body field causes a re-decorate per keystroke. Cheap in practice; deferred batched-refresh is a v1.x consideration if a wiki accumulates many rules.
