<$fill $name="body">

!! What it does

`rimir/mindmap` provides engine-agnostic mindmap rendering for TiddlyWiki. It defines a canonical mindmap document model (MDOM), separates ''data projection'' (producer modules that read wiki data) from ''visualization'' (engine adapters that draw it), and adds a per-view ''overlay'' layer where positioning and restructuring changes are stored without writing back to the underlying wiki data.

Inspired by the `flibbles/graph` + engine-adapter split (e.g. `cytoscape-engine`), but tree-shaped from the ground up — mindmap engines like mind-elixir take a recursive `{topic, children}` tree, not a flat node/edge list.

!! Key features

* ''Engine-agnostic'' — pluggable adapters via `module-type: mindmapengine`. Ships with no built-in engine; install a companion plugin such as `rimir/mindmap-elixir`.
* ''Three producer mechanisms'' — `module-type: mindmap-producer` modules, JSON MDOM tiddlers, or a `filter=` quick form. All feed the same canonical document.
* ''Base + overlay model'' — view-specific positioning, hides, reparenting and custom nodes ride in a separate overlay tiddler (ordered op log). Multiple views over the same base data are first-class.
* ''Structural editing (write-back)'' — producers can opt-in to mutate the underlying wiki: drag-rename / drag-reparent / addNode / removeNode become `renameTiddler` (with flibbles/relink cascade), `addTiddler`, `deleteTiddler`. Per-op routing keeps visual ops (collapse, sibling order) in the overlay.
* ''Focus mode'' — drill into a subtree; ↓/↑/⇪ buttons step in and out.
* ''Configurable label field'' — visible labels can be driven by `caption` (or any field) instead of title-path-suffix. Decouples display from structural identity.
* ''Cascade-confirm modal'' — guards large-effect operations: reparenting or deleting a subtree with more than ''N'' descendants pops a confirm dialog before applying.
* ''Stable IDs with rename rescue'' — producers assign deterministic IDs; orphaned overlay ops survive upstream renames and surface a manual prune action rather than silently disappearing.
* ''Slide authoring'' — each knowledge node can own zero-or-more slide tiddlers under `<owner>/slides/<slug>`, ordered by the owner's `mm.slide-order` TW list field. Slides carry their own `caption`, `mm.slide-layout`, `mm.slide-notes`, and the slide body as the tiddler's `text` — so every slide has its own created/modified timestamps, search visibility, and survives owner-renames via flibbles/relink-titles. A modebar at the top of the preview pane has an inspect-mode dropdown that swaps the body preview for a slide list with inline add/edit/move/delete.
* ''Slides-only view'' — a toolbar toggle prunes the canvas to the //presentation-eligible spine//: only nodes that have at least one slide, or whose descendants do. Composes with focus mode (focus narrows first, then the prune trims). Toggling off restores the full tree. Session-only state so the choice doesn't leak between browser windows.
* ''Named presentations (Phase 2)'' — playlists of nodes (tag `$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/presentation`, fields `mm.view` + `mm.slides-order`). The preview-pane modebar dropdown unifies mode + presentation picking (Body / Slides / each presentation / + New); per-node +/− button toggles membership; presentation mode renders the sequenced playback list with clickable node titles that focus the canvas.
* ''Fullscreen player (Phase 3C-i)'' — hands the active presentation off to the `rimir/present` plugin's `$present` widget for fullscreen playback. Compact ▶ button next to the modebar dropdown OR Shift+F2 from the canvas. New filter operator `[<pres>mm-presentation-slides[]]` flattens the presentation to its ordered slide tiddlers; a page-template tiddler gates the overlay on a state tiddler. Presentation //creation mode// on the canvas (fade non-included nodes, drag-reorder) is the remaining Phase 3 piece.

!! How it fits together

```
       Wiki tiddlers
            │
            ▼
   ┌────────────────┐    base MDOM      ┌──────────────┐
   │  producer (JS) │ ──────────────────▶  composer    │
   └────────────────┘                   │              │
            ▲                           │  base + ops  │  composite MDOM
            │ refreshFilter             │              │ ─────────────┐
            │                           └──────────────┘              │
            │                                  ▲                      ▼
   changes in matching                         │             ┌──────────────────┐
        tiddlers                          ops log            │  engine adapter  │
                                              ▲             └──────────────────┘
                                              │                      │
                                       overlay tiddler               ▼
                                              ▲                  DOM canvas
                                              │                      │
                                              └──────── op ──────────┘
                                                  (user gesture)
```

!! Prerequisites

* TiddlyWiki 5.3.0+
* An installed engine plugin (e.g. `$:/plugins/rimir/mindmap-elixir`).

</$fill>
</$transclude>

!! `<$mindmap>` widget

|!Attribute |!Default |!Purpose |
|`view` |— |Title of a view tiddler bundling producer + args + overlay + engine |
|`filter` |— |Quick-form: filter expression projected via the built-in `filter-tree` producer |
|`engine` |(config / first) |Engine name override |
|`overlay` |— |Overlay tiddler title (quick form only; view tiddler supplies its own) |
|`class` |— |Extra CSS class on the container `<div>` |
|`style` |— |Inline `style` attribute |
|`height` |— |Numeric height in px or any valid CSS length |
|`readonly` |`no` |If `yes`, user gestures do not write to the overlay |
|`state` |— |State-tiddler prefix for engine-internal UI state (reserved) |
|`onSelectActions` |— |Action string invoked on node selection; receives `<<nodeId>>` |
|`allow-node-creation` |`yes` |`no` to suppress the engine's native node-creation gestures (Tab → child, Enter → sibling, context-menu "Add Child"/"Add Sibling"). Useful for read-only / synthetic-structure views (e.g. `grouped-tree`) where new nodes have no tiddler-of-origin. View-tiddler `mm.allow-node-creation` is the fallback |
|`flags` |— |TW filter resolving to flag-rule tiddler titles (tagged `$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/flag`). Overrides the view-tiddler `mm.flags` field. Empty → no flags applied. See ''Flag decoration'' section below |

Setting both `view` and `filter` is a configuration error and renders an error banner.

!! View tiddler fields

|!Field |!Required |!Purpose |
|`mm.producer` |yes |Name of a registered `mindmap-producer` |
|`mm.args` |yes (JSON object) |Arguments passed to the producer |
|`mm.overlay` |no |Overlay tiddler title. Static; persists the engine's setAttr / reorder / hide ops (collapse/expand state, etc.). When `mm.overlay-filter` resolves to a non-empty title that one wins instead |
|`mm.overlay-filter` |no |TW filter evaluated in the widget's variable scope; the first result becomes the per-render overlay tiddler title. Use for per-entity persistence: with `<<entity>>` set by a parent `<$let>`, write `[<entity>!is[blank]addprefix[$:/saved-state/myplugin/]]`. Empty result falls back to `mm.overlay` |
|`mm.saved-default` |no |Static tiddler title holding the //view-wide// saved default state (a JSON array of overlay ops). Applied BEFORE the per-entity overlay at compose time — overlay ops override defaults. Toolbar's ''Save as default'' promotes the current overlay into this target. Without this field the toolbar's save / reset buttons are hidden |
|`mm.engine` |no |Engine name override |
|`mm.options` |no (JSON object) |Engine-specific options |
|`mm.id-aliases` |no (JSON object) |Old-id → new-id rescue map applied before composition |
|`mm.focus` |no |Initial focus title — re-roots the MDOM at that subtree on first render |
|`mm.label-field` |no |Tiddler field driving the visible node label. Default `title` uses the leaf-segment of the title; `caption` (or any field) decouples display from structural identity |
|`mm.presentation` |no |Title of the currently-active presentation tiddler for this view. Empty means "no presentation". Written by the preview-pane modebar dropdown when the user picks a presentation |
|`mm.allow-node-creation` |no |`yes` / `no`. Overridden by widget attr `allow-node-creation` when set. When `no`, the engine swallows native node-creation gestures (Tab/Enter and context-menu "Add Child"). Engine-agnostic — engines implement `setAllowNodeCreation(bool)` |
|`mm.root-label` |no |Override the producer's natural root label. ''Literal mode'': any non-empty string //not// starting with `[`. ''Filter mode'': starts with `[`. Evaluated in the widget's variable scope (parent `<$let>` variables are visible — write `[<entity>get[caption]] ~[<entity>]` to use the surrounding entity's caption). First filter result wins; empty falls back to the producer's default |
|`mm.preview-body-template` |no |Title of a wikitext tiddler rendered in the right pane's Body mode in place of the default text-view. Receives variables `<<previewTitle>>` (leaf selection's backing title), `<<previewKind>>` (synthetic-node chainId — empty for leaves), `<<previewKindAxisKey>>`, `<<previewKindKeyPath>>`. Branch on `previewKind` first to render kind-specific UI for chain/axis selections |
|`mm.flags` |no |TW filter resolving to flag-rule tiddler titles applied to this view. Overridden by the widget `flags=` attr when present. See ''Flag decoration'' section below |

!! Flag decoration

Flag rules apply filter-driven visual signals to nodes — icons, colour, border, font-weight, etc. — without producer changes. A rule is a plain tiddler tagged `$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/flag`; the widget runs each rule's filter once per render against the candidate leaf-titles (one wiki call per rule — //M filter calls//, not N×M) and stamps the matching nodes with MDOM attrs the engine adapter renders.

!!! Rule schema

|!Field |!Required |!Purpose |
|`mm.flag-name` |yes |Short slug `[a-z0-9-]`. Stamped as `data-mm-flags="<name>"` on the DOM (token-list — multiple flags coexist) and as the per-flag boolean attr `mx:flag-<name>` for finer CSS hooks |
|`mm.flag-filter` |yes |//Predicate filter// applied to the candidate leaf set. Use field operators directly (`[priority[critical]]`). //Do not// use `[is[current]…]` — the decorator passes the candidate titles as the filter's source, so `is[current]` doesn't fire. When chaining operators that //replace// the title with a derived value (e.g. `get[field]`, `oa-task-urgency[]`, `addsuffix[…]`), wrap the predicate in `:filter[…]` to preserve titles: `[rrt.type[task]] :filter[oa-task-urgency[]match[Past]]` |
|`mm.flag-aggregate` |no |`any` → stamp the rule on synthetic ancestors (`core:synthetic === true`) that have ≥1 matching leaf descendant. `all` → only when 100% of leaf descendants match. Empty → leaf-only (no aggregation). Non-synthetic ancestors are NEVER stamped by aggregation |
|`mm.flag-scope` |no |TW filter that gates rule eligibility. Evaluated once at load time with `<currentTiddler>` = the view tiddler title and `<<mm-producer>>` = the active producer name. Empty result → rule skipped. Example: `[<mm-producer>match[grouped-tree]]` restricts a rule to grouped-tree views |
|`mm.flag-priority` |no |Integer (default `0`). Higher priority applied LATER for style conflicts (last-wins) and appears EARLIER (leftmost) in the icon stack. Ties broken by source-tiddler title |
|`mm.flag-icon` |no |Single emoji / unicode glyph. Merged into the engine's icon array |
|`mm.flag-text-color` |no |CSS colour → `style.color` |
|`mm.flag-bg-color` |no |CSS colour. Writes `core:color` (reuses the existing background channel with auto-contrast foreground) |
|`mm.flag-border-color`, `mm.flag-border-width`, `mm.flag-border-style` |no |Component pieces composed into `mx:border` (`"2px solid #d04444"`). Mind-elixir adapter writes it to `style.outline` (NOT `border`) so the engine's focus ring still renders |
|`mm.flag-font-weight` |no |`bold`, `600`, etc. → `style.fontWeight` |
|`mm.flag-font-style` |no |`italic` → `style.fontStyle` |
|`mm.flag-text-transform` |no |`uppercase` / `lowercase` / `capitalize` → `style.textTransform` |
|`mm.flag-opacity` |no |`0.0`–`1.0`. Out-of-range values clamped with a console warning |
|`mm.flag-font-size-scale` |no |Multiplier like `1.15`. Adapter writes `style.fontSize = "<value>em"` |
|`mm.flag-class` |no |Extra class tokens appended to `data-mm-flag-classes`. CSS escape hatch when the schema doesn't cover a desired effect |
|`mm.flag-tooltip` |no |Text rendered in the topic's native `title=` tooltip. When multiple rules match a node, their tooltips stack on separate lines (ascending priority order). Combined with the producer's `core:tooltip` if both are set — `core:tooltip` first, then the flag block |

!!! Aggregation semantics

When a rule sets `mm.flag-aggregate`, the decorator walks the MDOM bottom-up after leaf decoration. Each synthetic ancestor's leaf-descendant count and matched-descendant count are memoised in one pass. Aggregation cascades naturally through nested synthetic levels (axis inside chain inside root). Recursion is capped at depth 64 with a console warning if exceeded — protects against malformed input.

A tiddler-backed parent (knowledge-tree's pattern of a note containing notes) is //not// considered synthetic and never picks up aggregated flags from its children. CSS can target the difference via `me-tpc[data-mm-synthetic="yes"]`.

!!! Stacking & conflict resolution

Rules sort ascending by `mm.flag-priority` (ties by source title). The decorator iterates ascending and:

* ''Names'' accumulate in ascending order: `mx:flags="r1 r2 r3"` (lowest priority first).
* ''Style attrs'' overwrite in ascending order: highest priority wins for the same property.
* ''Icons'' sort DESCENDING by priority before joining: `mx:icons="<highest>|<lower>|<lowest>"` (leftmost icon = most important).
* ''Classes'' concatenate (de-duplicated).

!!! DOM contract (mind-elixir adapter)

The adapter stamps three companion `data-*` attrs on `<me-tpc>` so CSS authors can style without engine-specific knowledge:

* `data-mm-flags="critical overdue"` — token list. Match individual flags with `me-tpc[data-mm-flags~="overdue"]`.
* `data-mm-flag-classes="kn-starred fade"` — custom class tokens from `mm.flag-class`.
* `data-mm-synthetic="yes"` — present on synthetic chain/axis nodes (regardless of flag state).

Plus the inline `style.*` properties driven by the `mx:*` attrs above. The first-class style channel means typography flags ("bold", "uppercase") work without writing any CSS.

!!! Performance

Inverted-loop evaluation: M wiki filter calls per render (one per rule against the full candidate-title universe), then a single MDOM walk for decoration and one bottom-up walk for aggregation. For typical views (N ≤ 200 leaves, M ≤ 10 rules) this is sub-10ms.

The widget watches `[tag[$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/flag]]` — editing any rule tiddler re-runs the decoration pass without rebuilding the engine.

!! Grouped-tree producer args

The `grouped-tree` producer is for "flat entity set + multiple grouping axes" views — e.g. meetings grouped by year/month and separately by state. Structural nodes are //volatile//: they have no tiddler of origin and are derived from leaves' field values. The shape of a view is declared by an ''axis template''.

|!Arg |!Default |!Purpose |
|`template` |— |//Required.// Title of the axis-template tiddler |
|`canvas-id` |`default` |Logical canvas key; scopes the runtime ''axes-disabled'' state tiddler. Multiple canvases sharing one template each keep their own toggle state |

!!! Template tiddler

|!Field |!Purpose |
|`mm.template-id` |Stable id (defaults to title) |
|`mm.template-caption` |Visible label of the root |
|`mm.leaf-filter` |//Required.// TW filter producing the leaf set |
|`mm.chains` |Ordered TW list of chain tiddler titles. Single chain → root collapses to the chain; multi-chain → synthetic root above the chain roots |
|`mm.initially-disabled-axes` |TW list of //axis-ids// (NOT titles) initially toggled off. Overridden at runtime by the state tiddler |
|`mm.initially-collapsed-axes` |TW list of //axis-ids// whose group nodes render collapsed (`core:collapsed: true`) on first draw |
|`mm.initially-collapsed-chains` |TW list of //chain-ids// whose chain-root renders collapsed on first draw |
|`mm.show-counts` |`yes` to append ` (N)` to every synthetic node's label, where N is the descendant leaf count. Each synthetic node also carries `gt:leaf-count` for engines that want to render counts separately |

!!! Chain tiddler

|!Field |!Purpose |
|`mm.chain-id` |Stable id (defaults to title) |
|`mm.chain-caption` |Label of the chain's synthetic root |
|`mm.leaf-filter` |Optional predicate-style filter narrowing the template's leaf set before any axis or sub-chain in this chain runs. Evaluated per-leaf — write `[get[rrt.type]match[meeting]]` not `:filter[...]`. //Gotcha//: the leaf arrives via the //source iterator//, so do NOT lead a run with `<currentTiddler>` — it would resolve to the //widget's// currentTiddler (the surrounding view tiddler), not the leaf. Use the bare operator form (`[get[…]]`) and let the iterator provide the implicit input. Outer widget vars like `<entity>` //do// resolve correctly (e.g. `[<entity>get[rrt.type]match[person]]`) |
|`mm.leaf-sort` |Optional TW filter applied to the chain's filtered leaves before they enter the axis pipeline. Input is the leaf list; output is the same list reordered. Within each axis bucket, leaves appear in this sort order (`groupBy` preserves first-seen). Examples: `[nsort[datetime]reverse[]]` (newest-first for meetings), `[has[due-date]nsort[due-date]] [!has[due-date]]` (most-urgent first, blanks last). //Fail-safe semantics//: a sort that returns empty (e.g. typo, impossible predicate) keeps input order; titles outside the input set are dropped; input leaves the sort filter drops are appended in their input-relative order so no leaf vanishes |
|`mm.axes` |Ordered TW list of axis tiddler titles — //leaf chain// (terminal, applies the axis pipeline) |
|`mm.sub-chains` |Ordered TW list of CHILD chain tiddler titles — //parent chain// (renders each sub-chain as a synthetic child under this chain's root; the parent's filtered leaf set cascades into every sub-chain). When both `mm.axes` and `mm.sub-chains` are set, sub-chains win |
|`mm.chain-hide-when-empty` |`yes` to omit the chain entirely when its filtered leaf set is empty AND it has no rendering child chains. Use for chains that only make sense for certain entity types (e.g. orga-apps' Topics chain renders only when the view's `<entity>` is a person or team) so other entity types don't paint an empty "(0)" branch. Default off (legacy: empty chains render as a clickable bucket showing 0 leaves) |

!!! Axis tiddler

|!Field |!Purpose |
|`mm.axis-id` |//Required.// Stable id referenced from `mm.initially-disabled-axes` and the runtime state tiddler |
|`mm.axis-caption` |Human-readable label of the axis (not yet rendered in the canvas) |
|`mm.axis-field` |Leaf field whose value is the group key. Used when `mm.axis-derive` is absent |
|`mm.axis-derive` |TW filter computing the key from the leaf (currentTiddler = leaf title; first result wins). Overrides `mm.axis-field` when both present |
|`mm.axis-label-template` |Label template for the group node. ''Literal mode'' (default): `<<key>>` is substituted with the raw key. ''Filter mode'' (starts with `[`): evaluated as a TW filter with the `key` variable bound; first result becomes the label. Falls back to the raw key when the filter yields nothing |
|`mm.axis-create-defaults` |JSON field→value map applied when a leaf is created under this axis (Phase B — not yet active) |
|`mm.axis-leaf-filter` |Optional filter; leaves failing this filter are dropped from the chain at this depth |
|`mm.axis-sort` |Sort order for the axis's group nodes: `first-seen` (default — insertion order), `asc` (alpha), `desc` (alpha reversed — useful for dates newest-first), `enum` (explicit order via `mm.axis-sort-keys`) |
|`mm.axis-sort-keys` |For `mm.axis-sort: enum`. Ordered TW list of expected key values. Keys not listed sort after the enum in alphabetical order |

!!! Runtime override

Toggling an axis at runtime writes a session-scoped state tiddler:

```
$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<canvas-id>/axes-disabled
```

Body is a TW list of axis-ids. ''When present, it fully replaces the template's `initially-disabled-axes`'' — no merge. Absence falls back to the template defaults. `$:/state/` tiddlers don't sync, so this keeps git clean.

!!! Node id namespaces

|!Pattern |!Used for |
|`gt:__root__` |Synthetic root (multi-chain only) |
|`gt:__empty__` |Empty / error placeholder root |
|`gt:chain:<chainId>` |Chain synthetic root |
|`gt:axis:<chainId>:<keyPath>` |Axis group node. `<keyPath>` is the pipe-joined cumulative axis-key path from the chain root, so the same key under different ancestors (e.g. "Jan" under 2026 vs 2025) yields distinct ids. The current axis-id is preserved in the `gt:axis-id` attr |
|`gt:leaf:<title>@<chainId>` |Leaf //occurrence//. The same tiddler appears once per chain; `core:tiddler` attr carries the underlying title |

!! Knowledge-tree producer args

|!Arg |!Default |!Purpose |
|`area` |— |Required when `include-areas-root` is `no`. Knowledge area id (e.g. `llm`) — determines the title prefix used as the tree root |
|`delimiter` |`/` |Path delimiter |
|`area-tag` |`$:/tags/rimir/knowledge-app/area` |Tag identifying area tiddlers. Override to host a parallel set of areas (e.g. `$:/tags/rimir/priv-app/knowledge-area` for priv-app's private knowledge trees) without polluting the public knowledge-app area list. Forest mode and single-area mode both honour this tag |
|`root-prefix` |`knowledge` |Title-path root above the area id. Default `knowledge` → tree lives at `knowledge/<area>/…`. Set to e.g. `private/knowledge` to host trees at `private/knowledge/<area>/…`. Multi-segment values are split on `delimiter`. Threaded through `produce()`, `rootTitle()`, and `refreshFilter()`; `applyOps` is unaffected because it operates on the node's full title |
|`include-areas-root` |`no` |If `yes`, build a forest of all areas under a synthetic "Knowledge" root |
|`label-field` |`title` |Tiddler field driving the visible node label (see view fields) |
|`focus-title` |— |Re-root the MDOM at this subtree. Composes with `slides-only` (re-root first, then prune) |
|`slides-only` |`no` |If `yes`, prune the tree to nodes with at least one slide or with slide-bearing descendants. Surface via the toolbar toggle, not direct view-tiddler config |

!! Producer module contract

```
title: $:/your-plugin/producers/foo.js
type: application/javascript
module-type: mindmap-producer

exports.name           = "foo";
exports.produce        = function (args, wiki, widget) → MDOM;   // required
exports.refreshFilter  = function (args) → string                // optional
exports.describe       = function () → { name, args: [...] }    // optional

// Structural editing — opt-in:
exports.capabilities   = { structural: true, structuralOps: ["rename", "reparent", "addNode", "removeNode"], slides: true };
exports.applyOps       = function (ops, args, wiki) → results[]; // mutates the wiki
exports.titleForOp     = function (op) → string|null;            // for cascade counting
exports.idForTitle     = function (title) → string|null;         // inverse of titleForOp; used by presentation click-to-select
exports.rootTitle      = function (args) → string|null;          // for step-out detection

// Synthetic-node preview classifier — opt-in:
exports.previewKindForId = function (id) → { kind, chainId, axisKey?, keyPath? } | null;
```

A producer that emits structural nodes that aren't tiddlers (chain roots, axis groups, etc.) can implement `previewKindForId`. When the user selects such a node, the widget writes the returned descriptor to `$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<key>/preview-kind` and the host preview-body template can branch on `<<previewKind>>` (the `chainId`) to render kind-specific UI — e.g. the same list view the user sees on a dedicated tab. Leaf selections continue to populate `<<previewTitle>>`.

Producers MUST emit deterministic node IDs (prefixed with a producer-unique namespace). IDs are the join key between base and overlay.

''Structural producers'' route rename / reparent / addNode / removeNode through `applyOps`; all other ops still land in the overlay. `applyOps` results may carry `collisionResolved: true` (slug uniquified — surfaced to the user as a toast).

''Slides-capable producers'' (`capabilities.slides: true`) understand the `slides-only` produce arg and prune their output tree accordingly. The widget shows the ''Slides only'' toolbar toggle only when this capability is set.

!! Engine adapter contract

```
title: $:/your-engine/adapter.js
type: application/javascript
module-type: mindmapengine

exports.name         = "MindElixir";
exports.capabilities = { applyOps: false, focus: true, expand: true, drag: true, edit: false };
exports.init         = function (element, mdom, options);
exports.update       = function (mdom);
exports.applyOps     = function (ops);                  // optional
exports.focus        = function (nodeId);
exports.expand       = function (nodeId);
exports.collapse     = function (nodeId);
exports.on           = function (event, fn);            // events: op, select
exports.destroy      = function ();
```

If the adapter exports a constructor (function), the widget calls `new Engine(wiki)`. Otherwise the exported object is used directly.

The adapter MUST:
* Deep-clone the MDOM before mutating it (some engines like mind-elixir mutate their input).
* Preserve unknown-namespace `attrs` keys across `update()`.
* Release global listeners in `destroy()`.

The adapter SHOULD:
* Translate native gesture events into the canonical Op vocabulary before emitting `on("op", ...)`.
* Suppress duplicate `setAttr` ops on the same id/key during drag (the overlay store coalesces these as a safety net, but emit fewer if possible).

!! Op vocabulary (overlay log)

```
{ op: "hide",       id: string }
{ op: "rename",     id: string, label: string }
{ op: "setAttr",    id: string, key: string, value: any }
{ op: "reparent",   id: string, newParent: string, index?: number }
{ op: "reorder",    parent: string, order: string[] }
{ op: "addNode",    parent: string, node: MNode, index?: number }
{ op: "removeNode", id: string }
```

!! Filter operators

|!Operator |!Returns |
|`[mindmap-engines[]]` |Names of all registered `mindmapengine` modules |
|`[mindmap-producers[]]` |Names of all registered `mindmap-producer` modules |
|`[<owner>mm-slides[]]` |Ordered slide tiddler titles for the given owner (reads `mm.slide-order`; stale entries dropped) |
|`[<owner>mm-slide-count[]]` |Number of slides on the given owner |
|`[<owner>mm-has-slides[]]` |`yes` / `no` — does this owner have at least one slide |
|`[<pres>mm-presentation-slides[]]` |Flat ordered list of slide tiddler titles for a presentation. Walks the presentation's `mm.slides-order` and, per owner node, emits each slide in `mm.slide-order` order. Designed to feed `<$present slides=…/>` from `rimir/present` |
|`[mm-presentations<viewTitle>]` |Titles of presentation tiddlers (tag `$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/presentation`) whose `mm.view` matches the operand |

!! Widgets

|!Tag |!Purpose |
|`<$mindmap>` |The mindmap canvas + preview pane. See attribute table above. |

!! Tag conventions

|!Tag |!Purpose |
|`$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/presentation` |Marks a tiddler as a presentation playlist. Required fields: `mm.view` (associated view), `mm.slides-order` (ordered TW list of member tiddler titles). Optional: `mm.transition`, `mm.duration`, `caption` (for the toolbar dropdown label) |
|`$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/slide` |Marks a tiddler as one slide of an owning knowledge node (v0.2.7+). Stored at `<owner>/slides/<slug>`. Required fields: `kn.type=slide`, `mm.slide-of=<owner-title>`, body as `text`. Optional: `caption`, `mm.slide-layout` (`default`/`title`/`bullets`/...), `mm.slide-notes`. The owner's `mm.slide-order` TW list field drives display order |

!! Config tiddlers

|!Tiddler |!Default |!Purpose |
|`$:/config/rimir/mindmap/default-engine` |(first registered) |Fallback engine name when widget and view don't specify |
|`$:/config/rimir/mindmap/structural/new-node-type-strategy` |`fixed:note` |`fixed:<type>` or `derive-from-parent`. Chooses `kn.type` of nodes created via `+child` / `+sibling` |
|`$:/config/rimir/mindmap/structural/new-node-type-default` |`note` |Fallback type when `derive-from-parent` finds no parent type |
|`$:/config/rimir/mindmap/structural/cascade-threshold` |`10` |Rename/reparent/delete affecting more than this many descendants pops a confirm modal |
|`$:/config/rimir/mindmap/label-fields` |`title\ncaption` |Newline-separated list of tiddler fields shown in the actions-panel label-field dropdown |

!! Session state tiddlers

|!Tiddler |!Purpose |
|`$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<key>/focus-title` |Currently focused subtree (session-only — `$:/state/` doesn't sync) |
|`$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<key>/label-field` |Session override for the visible-label field |
|`$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<key>/inspect-mode` |`body` (default), `slides`, or `presentation` — controls what the preview pane renders |
|`$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<key>/slide-editing` |Title of the slide tiddler currently being edited inline (empty = list view) |
|`$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<key>/slides-only` |`yes` when the canvas is pruned to slide-bearing nodes (toolbar toggle) — empty otherwise |
|`$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<key>/preview-selected` |Currently selected node id (for the preview pane) |
|`$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<key>/preview-edit-mode` |`yes` while the preview is in inline-edit mode |
|`$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<key>/breadcrumb-history` |List-field of titles visited via in-preview link clicks. Pushed on link-click, reset on canvas selection, truncated on breadcrumb item click |
|`$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<key>/pending-select` |Title written by an external-jump "Follow" from another mindmap. Consumed once after engine init (`consumePendingSelect`), then cleared |
|`$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<key>/open-in-new-tab` |Per-widget bridge written by the external-jump modal's "Open in new tab" branch; the widget's `refresh()` reads and clears, then calls `window.open(…, "_blank")` |
|`$:/state/rimir/mindmap/pending-cascade` |JSON of the deferred op + count + widget key |
|`$:/state/rimir/mindmap/pending-cascade-apply` |`yes` when the user confirms the deferred op |
|`$:/state/rimir/mindmap/external-jump/pending` |Modal trigger written by `handlePreviewLinkClick` when an out-of-subtree click matches a tagged-config mapping. Fields: `target-title`, `mapping-title`, `target-label`, `widget-key` |

`<key>` is the widget's `state=` attribute, else its `view=` / `filter=` value, else `default`. Multiple `$mindmap` widgets sharing a key share state — useful for embedded toolbars, harmful for embedded copies of the same view.

!! Widget messages

|!Message |!Param |!Purpose |
|`rr-mindmap-select-node-by-title` |`{title}` paramObject |Select a node by its backing tiddler title. Used by the presentation pane's playlist click-to-select |
|`rr-mindmap-breadcrumb-jump` |1-based `param` index |Truncate the link-history breadcrumb to the clicked position and select that node |
|`rr-mindmap-open-in-new-tab` |`param` title (or `{title}` paramObject) |Bridge for wikitext callers (inside the widget tree) to invoke `openInNewTab(title)` — uses the appify-safe permalink + `target="_blank"` |
|`rr-mindmap-add-slide` |`{owner}` paramObject |Create a blank slide tiddler under the owner and open it in inline-edit mode |
|`tm-navigate` |native `navigateTo` |Intercepted by `handlePreviewLinkClick` when origin is inside the preview pane; classifies into in-subtree / in-subtree-missing / out-of-subtree paths |

!! External-jump tag schema

Tiddlers tagged `$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/external-jump` define title-prefix → destination mappings for the preview-pane's out-of-subtree click handler. Longest matching `title-prefix` wins (so a more specific mapping can override a generic one).

|!Field |!Required |!Purpose |
|`title-prefix` |yes |Match string. The clicked target matches when `target === prefix` OR `target.startsWith(prefix + "/")` |
|`target-label` |yes |Human-readable label shown in the modal ("Follow → <label>") |
|`target-actions` |yes |Wikitext action chain fired on Follow. Typically `<$action-statewrap-set>` to switch appify channels |
|`target-view` |no |View-tiddler title (e.g. `Mindmap/private-fitness`). When set, the clicked target title is written to `$:/state/rimir/mindmap/<target-view>/pending-select` so the destination mindmap auto-selects the linked node on its next render |

</$fill>
</$transclude>

<$fill $name="body">

!! Module-type discovery

The widget calls `$tw.modules.getModulesByTypeAsHashmap("mindmapengine")` and `"mindmap-producer"` at render time. The hashmap key is the JS module's tiddler title; the value is the exports object. Names are deduplicated via `exports.name`. Module-type registration only happens at boot — adding a new producer or engine requires a server restart.

!! `<$transclude>` and `thisTiddler`

In TW 5.4.0+, `<$transclude $tiddler="X" $mode="block"/>` sets `thisTiddler`, not `currentTiddler`. Producers that resolve "the rendering context" from filters should read both:

```
{{{ [<thisTiddler>!is[blank]] ~[<currentTiddler>] }}}
```

The `$mindmap` widget itself doesn't expose this variable to producers in v1, but custom producers running inside a transclude chain should be defensive.

!! `\function` fake-widget context

If a custom producer evaluates filter expressions that walk the widget tree (e.g. `statewrap-get`), use `\procedure` + `[subfilter<...>]` inside the producer's body, not `\function` + `[function[...]]`. The fake widget created by `\function` has no `parentWidget` chain.

!! Hook chain safety

The widget does not install any `th-*` hooks. If a future feature needs to listen for tiddler change/delete, it must `return tiddler` from the hook (per the well-known gotcha that breaks the entire hook chain when any plugin forgets).

!! filesystem-watcher / git-int interactions

Every overlay write triggers a tiddler change → filesystem-watcher writes the file → git-int notices a dirty working tree. We debounce overlay writes at 250 ms, and adapters MUST collapse drag gestures to start/end pairs instead of emitting `setAttr` per pointermove. If you see git-int spamming with intermediate positions, the adapter is the bug.

!! Restricted-wiki implications

In `llm-connect` or other restricted-wiki environments, overlay tiddler titles must be in the protection allow filter. Writes to titles outside the filter are silently dropped (no exception). The settings tab documents this; the widget cannot detect it client-side.

!! TestCaseWidget pollution

The `test/` fixtures use `tags: $:/tags/wiki-test-spec`. Tests that addTiddler from the browser will land in `pw-edition/tiddlers/` (gitignored) and shadow plugin tiddlers in subsequent runs. Always clean up in `afterEach` or use disposable state titles.

!! Code-body parsing

The `views.tid` and `producers.tid` tool tabs use `\procedure` pragmas. They MUST NOT carry `code-body: yes` or pragmas become literal text. See `tw-wikitext-gotchas.md` in the project memory for the full list.

</$fill>
</$transclude>

title: $:/plugins/rimir/mindmap/filters/helpers.js
type: application/javascript
module-type: filteroperator

Filter operators exposing the registered engines and producers so the
settings/tools UI can list them without reflecting on $tw.modules from
wikitext.

  [[mindmap-engines[]]]      — names of all registered mindmapengine modules
  [[mindmap-producers[]]]    — names of all registered mindmap-producer modules

The input list is ignored; both operators emit a fresh list of names.

\*/

"use strict";

function listNames(moduleType) {
    var modules = $tw.modules.getModulesByTypeAsHashmap(moduleType);
    var names = [];
    for (var key in modules) {
        var mod = modules[key];
        if (mod && mod.name) { names.push(mod.name); }
    }
    names.sort();
    return names;
}

exports["mindmap-engines"] = function (source, operator, options) {
    return listNames("mindmapengine");
};

exports["mindmap-producers"] = function (source, operator, options) {
    return listNames("mindmap-producer");
};
","type":"application/javascript","module-type":"filteroperator"},"$:/plugins/rimir/mindmap/filters/presentation.js":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/mindmap/filters/presentation.js","text":"/*\
title: $:/plugins/rimir/mindmap/filters/presentation.js
type: application/javascript
module-type: filteroperator

Filter operators for named-presentation discovery.

  [mm-presentations<viewTitle>]
      Lists titles of presentation tiddlers (tagged
      `$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/presentation`) whose `mm.view` field equals
      the given view title. Sorted alphabetically by title.

      Example: [mm-presentations<currentTiddler>]

\*/

"use strict";

var PRESENTATION_TAG = "$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/presentation";

exports["mm-presentations"] = function (source, operator, options) {
    var viewTitle = (operator.operand || "").replace(/^\s+|\s+$/g, "");
    if (!viewTitle) { return []; }
    var results = [];
    options.wiki.each(function (tiddler, title) {
        if (!tiddler || !tiddler.fields) { return; }
        var tags = $tw.utils.parseStringArray(tiddler.fields.tags || "");
        if (tags.indexOf(PRESENTATION_TAG) < 0) { return; }
        var view = (tiddler.fields["mm.view"] || "").replace(/^\s+|\s+$/g, "");
        if (view === viewTitle) { results.push(title); }
    });
    results.sort();
    return results;
};
","type":"application/javascript","module-type":"filteroperator"},"$:/plugins/rimir/mindmap/filters/sanitize.js":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/mindmap/filters/sanitize.js","text":"/*\
title: $:/plugins/rimir/mindmap/filters/sanitize.js
type: application/javascript
module-type: filteroperator

Filter operator that converts each input title into a sanitised slug, using
the same rules as the structural-producer write-back path.

Usage:
    [[My Label]mindmap-slug[]]      → "my-label"
    [<label>mindmap-slug[]]          → slug of <label>

\*/

"use strict";

var sanitizeLib = require("$:/plugins/rimir/mindmap/lib/sanitize-title.js");

exports["mindmap-slug"] = function (source, operator, options) {
    var results = [];
    source(function (tiddler, title) {
        var slug = sanitizeLib.sanitize(title);
        if (slug !== null) { results.push(slug); }
    });
    return results;
};
","type":"application/javascript","module-type":"filteroperator"},"$:/plugins/rimir/mindmap/filters/slides.js":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/mindmap/filters/slides.js","text":"/*\
title: $:/plugins/rimir/mindmap/filters/slides.js
type: application/javascript
module-type: filteroperator

Filter operators exposing the slide-tiddler model (v0.2.7+) to wikitext.

  [<owner>mm-slides[]]        — ordered slide tiddler titles for one or more
                                 owner tiddlers (skips titles that no longer
                                 resolve to slide tiddlers — defensive against
                                 stale order entries).
  [<owner>mm-slide-count[]]   — number of slides each owner has.
  [<owner>mm-has-slides[]]    — "yes" if the owner has at least one slide,
                                 "no" otherwise.
  [<pres>mm-presentation-slides[]]
                              — flat ordered list of slide tiddler titles for
                                 a presentation tiddler. Walks the
                                 presentation's `mm.slides-order` (owner
                                 nodes) and emits each owner's `mm-slides`
                                 in order. Designed to feed `<$present>`.

INPUT: one or more owner tiddler titles. Each yields zero-or-more outputs
(slide titles for mm-slides; one count for mm-slide-count; one yes/no for
mm-has-slides; many slide titles for mm-presentation-slides).

\*/

"use strict";

var slideTiddlers = require("$:/plugins/rimir/mindmap/lib/slide-tiddlers.js");

function trim(s) { return (s || "").replace(/^\s+|\s+$/g, ""); }

exports["mm-slides"] = function (source, operator, options) {
    var results = [];
    source(function (tiddler, title) {
        var slides = slideTiddlers.getSlideTitles(options.wiki, title);
        for (var i = 0; i < slides.length; i++) { results.push(slides[i]); }
    });
    return results;
};

exports["mm-slide-count"] = function (source, operator, options) {
    var results = [];
    source(function (tiddler, title) {
        var slides = slideTiddlers.getSlideTitles(options.wiki, title);
        results.push(String(slides.length));
    });
    return results;
};

exports["mm-has-slides"] = function (source, operator, options) {
    var results = [];
    source(function (tiddler, title) {
        var slides = slideTiddlers.getSlideTitles(options.wiki, title);
        results.push(slides.length > 0 ? "yes" : "no");
    });
    return results;
};

// Flat ordered list of slide tiddlers for a presentation tiddler. Each input
// title is treated as a presentation; we read its `mm.slides-order` (owner
// node titles) and concatenate each owner's `getSlideTitles` in list order.
// Owners that don't exist or have no slides are skipped silently.
exports["mm-presentation-slides"] = function (source, operator, options) {
    var results = [];
    source(function (tiddler, title) {
        var pres = options.wiki.getTiddler(title);
        if (!pres || !pres.fields) { return; }
        var orderRaw = trim(pres.fields["mm.slides-order"] || "");
        if (!orderRaw) { return; }
        var owners = $tw.utils.parseStringArray(orderRaw);
        for (var i = 0; i < owners.length; i++) {
            var slides = slideTiddlers.getSlideTitles(options.wiki, owners[i]);
            for (var j = 0; j < slides.length; j++) { results.push(slides[j]); }
        }
    });
    return results;
};
","type":"application/javascript","module-type":"filteroperator"},"$:/plugins/rimir/mindmap/flags":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/mindmap/flags","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"! Flag rules — filter-driven visual signals

''Flag rules'' attach icons, colour, border, font-weight, and other visual signals to mindmap nodes based on a TW filter. Authors write rules as plain tiddlers tagged `$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/flag`; the widget runs each rule's filter once per render and stamps matching leaves (plus, optionally, their synthetic ancestors).

!! Quickstart

Create a rule tiddler:

```
title:           $:/my-flags/critical
tags:            $:/tags/rimir/mindmap/flag
mm.flag-name:    critical
mm.flag-filter:  [priority[critical]]
mm.flag-icon:    🔥
mm.flag-font-weight: bold
mm.flag-aggregate:   any
mm.flag-priority:    30
```

Opt the view in:

```
mm.flags: [tag[$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/flag]]
```

Or per-widget:

```
<$mindmap view="..." flags="[tag[$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/flag]]"/>
```

The default (empty `mm.flags`, no `flags=`) applies //no// flags — opt-in only.

!! Full schema, recipes, gotchas

See the ''Flags'' tab in the plugin's Documentation hub (rendered via the doc-template plugin) or the //Reference// tab's ''Flag decoration'' section.

!! Listing rules in the current wiki

<$list filter="[tag[$:/tags/rimir/mindmap/flag]]" emptyMessage="(no flag rules in this wiki)">
* <$link to=<<currentTiddler>>><<currentTiddler>></$link> — name: <$transclude $tiddler=<<currentTiddler>> $field="mm.flag-name"/>, filter: `<$transclude $tiddler=<<currentTiddler>> $field="mm.flag-filter"/>`
</$list>

title: $:/plugins/rimir/mindmap/lib/flag-decorate.js
type: application/javascript
module-type: library

Filter-driven flag decoration for the mindmap MDOM.

Two responsibilities, exposed as pure-ish functions:

  loadFlagRules(wiki, opts) → [Rule]
      Resolve the candidate rule-tiddler titles from a TW filter, read each
      rule's fields, drop rules whose scope filter excludes the current
      view/producer, normalise field types, sort ascending by priority.

  decorateFlags(mdom, rules, wiki) → mdom    (mutated in place)
      For each rule, evaluate its filter ONCE over the universe of leaf
      titles (inverted loop — M filter calls, not N×M). Stamp the matching
      leaves with mx:flags / mx:icons / mx:flag-classes plus first-class
      style attrs (mx:text-color, mx:font-weight, mx:border → outline, …).
      If any rule declares aggregation, also walk bottom-up and stamp
      synthetic ancestors (core:synthetic === true) whose leaf-descendant
      counts satisfy the rule's `any` / `all` policy.

Engine-neutral: emits only MDOM attrs. The mind-elixir adapter is the only
component that translates those into DOM `data-*` attrs and inline `style.*`.
A future engine adapter can read the same attrs and render its own way.

\*/

"use strict";

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Rule loader

// Trim is mandatory: .tid field bodies often carry trailing newlines, and
// TW's filter parser silently no-ops on a name with a surprise " " or "\n".
function trim(s) { return (s === null || s === undefined) ? "" : String(s).replace(/^\s+|\s+$/g, ""); }

// Defensive lookup that tolerates wiki implementations exposing fields via
// `tiddler.fields` (in-tree wiki) vs `tiddler.getFieldString` (older test mocks).
function fieldOf(tiddler, name) {
    if (!tiddler) { return ""; }
    if (tiddler.fields && Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(tiddler.fields, name)) {
        return tiddler.fields[name];
    }
    if (typeof tiddler.getFieldString === "function") {
        return tiddler.getFieldString(name);
    }
    return "";
}

// Build a widget-like object the wiki filter engine can query for variables.
// Two anchors we expose:
//   currentTiddler = the view tiddler title (so scope filters reading
//                    <<currentTiddler>> see the view, not a leaf — see gotcha
//                    in plan)
//   mm-producer    = the producer module name (so a rule can scope itself
//                    to a specific producer with [<mm-producer>match[...]])
function makeScopeWidget(viewTitle, mmProducer) {
    var vars = { "currentTiddler": viewTitle || "", "mm-producer": mmProducer || "" };
    return {
        getVariable: function (name) {
            return Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(vars, name) ? vars[name] : "";
        }
    };
}

/*
 * loadFlagRules(wiki, opts) → [Rule]
 *
 * opts:
 *   rulesFilter : string   — TW filter resolving to flag-rule tiddler titles
 *                            (mm.flags view field or `flags=` widget attr)
 *   viewTitle   : string   — used as currentTiddler in mm.flag-scope eval
 *   mmProducer  : string   — exposed as <<mm-producer>> in mm.flag-scope
 *
 * Returns a sorted (ascending priority, ties broken by source title) list of
 * normalised Rule objects. Invalid rules are skipped with a console warning.
 */
exports.loadFlagRules = function (wiki, opts) {
    opts = opts || {};
    var rulesFilter = trim(opts.rulesFilter);
    if (!rulesFilter || !wiki || typeof wiki.filterTiddlers !== "function") { return []; }

    var titles;
    try {
        titles = wiki.filterTiddlers(rulesFilter) || [];
    } catch (e) {
        console.error("[mindmap-flags] rules filter failed: " + rulesFilter, e);
        return [];
    }

    var scopeWidget = makeScopeWidget(opts.viewTitle, opts.mmProducer);
    var rules = [];

    for (var i = 0; i < titles.length; i++) {
        var title = titles[i];
        var tiddler = wiki.getTiddler(title);
        if (!tiddler) { continue; }

        var name = trim(fieldOf(tiddler, "mm.flag-name"));
        if (!name) {
            console.warn("[mindmap-flags] rule '" + title + "' missing mm.flag-name; skipped");
            continue;
        }
        var filter = trim(fieldOf(tiddler, "mm.flag-filter"));
        if (!filter) {
            console.warn("[mindmap-flags] rule '" + title + "' missing mm.flag-filter; skipped");
            continue;
        }

        var scope = trim(fieldOf(tiddler, "mm.flag-scope"));
        if (scope) {
            try {
                var scoped = wiki.filterTiddlers(scope, scopeWidget) || [];
                if (scoped.length === 0) { continue; }
            } catch (e2) {
                console.error("[mindmap-flags] rule '" + name + "' scope filter failed", e2);
                continue;
            }
        }

        var priorityRaw = trim(fieldOf(tiddler, "mm.flag-priority"));
        var priority = priorityRaw === "" ? 0 : parseFloat(priorityRaw);
        if (isNaN(priority)) {
            console.warn("[mindmap-flags] rule '" + name + "' invalid priority '" + priorityRaw + "'; defaulting to 0");
            priority = 0;
        }

        var aggregate = trim(fieldOf(tiddler, "mm.flag-aggregate"));
        if (aggregate && aggregate !== "any" && aggregate !== "all") {
            console.warn("[mindmap-flags] rule '" + name + "' invalid aggregate '" + aggregate + "'; treating as leaf-only");
            aggregate = "";
        }

        var opacityRaw = trim(fieldOf(tiddler, "mm.flag-opacity"));
        var opacity = "";
        if (opacityRaw !== "") {
            var op = parseFloat(opacityRaw);
            if (isNaN(op)) {
                console.warn("[mindmap-flags] rule '" + name + "' invalid opacity '" + opacityRaw + "'; ignoring");
            } else {
                if (op < 0 || op > 1) {
                    console.warn("[mindmap-flags] rule '" + name + "' opacity out of [0,1]; clamping");
                    op = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, op));
                }
                opacity = String(op);
            }
        }

        rules.push({
            name: name,
            filter: filter,
            aggregate: aggregate,
            priority: priority,
            sourceTitle: title,
            "mm.flag-icon": trim(fieldOf(tiddler, "mm.flag-icon")),
            "mm.flag-text-color": trim(fieldOf(tiddler, "mm.flag-text-color")),
            "mm.flag-bg-color": trim(fieldOf(tiddler, "mm.flag-bg-color")),
            "mm.flag-border-color": trim(fieldOf(tiddler, "mm.flag-border-color")),
            "mm.flag-border-width": trim(fieldOf(tiddler, "mm.flag-border-width")),
            "mm.flag-border-style": trim(fieldOf(tiddler, "mm.flag-border-style")),
            "mm.flag-font-weight": trim(fieldOf(tiddler, "mm.flag-font-weight")),
            "mm.flag-font-style": trim(fieldOf(tiddler, "mm.flag-font-style")),
            "mm.flag-text-transform": trim(fieldOf(tiddler, "mm.flag-text-transform")),
            "mm.flag-opacity": opacity,
            "mm.flag-font-size-scale": trim(fieldOf(tiddler, "mm.flag-font-size-scale")),
            "mm.flag-class": trim(fieldOf(tiddler, "mm.flag-class")),
            "mm.flag-tooltip": trim(fieldOf(tiddler, "mm.flag-tooltip"))
        });
    }

    rules.sort(function (a, b) {
        if (a.priority !== b.priority) { return a.priority - b.priority; }
        return a.sourceTitle.localeCompare(b.sourceTitle);
    });

    return rules;
};

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Decoration

// Build title → [node] for every node carrying a non-empty `core:tiddler`.
// A single title may appear in multiple nodes (rare, but possible — focus mode
// can root the same tiddler twice). We stamp ALL such nodes from one matched
// result so the user sees consistent flags wherever the tiddler shows up.
function collectTitledNodes(root) {
    var byTitle = Object.create(null);
    var allTitled = [];   // ordered list of titled nodes — used by aggregation
    function walk(node) {
        if (!node) { return; }
        var attrs = node.attrs || {};
        var title = attrs["core:tiddler"];
        if (title) {
            if (!byTitle[title]) { byTitle[title] = []; }
            byTitle[title].push(node);
            allTitled.push({ node: node, title: title });
        }
        var children = node.children || [];
        for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) { walk(children[i]); }
    }
    walk(root);
    return { byTitle: byTitle, allTitled: allTitled };
}

// Parse "2px solid #d04444" → { width, style, color }. Each component may be
// missing — we just treat missing pieces as defaults during composition.
function parseBorderComposite(s) {
    if (!s) { return {}; }
    var parts = String(s).trim().split(/\s+/);
    var out = {};
    for (var i = 0; i < parts.length; i++) {
        var p = parts[i];
        if (/^\d/.test(p)) { out.width = p; }
        else if (/^(solid|dashed|dotted|double|groove|ridge|inset|outset)$/.test(p)) { out.style = p; }
        else { out.color = p; }
    }
    return out;
}

// Apply an ordered (ascending-priority) list of rules to a single MDOM node,
// merging their visual contributions into the node's attrs map. Idempotent in
// the sense that calling it a second time with the same rules yields the same
// resulting attrs.
//
// Stacking rules:
//   - mx:flags        : space-separated names, ascending priority order.
//   - mx:flag-<name>  : boolean true for each matching rule.
//   - mx:flag-classes : space-separated class tokens (de-duped).
//   - mx:icons        : pipe-separated chars, DESCENDING priority order
//                       (highest-priority icon appears leftmost in the topic).
//   - style attrs     : last-write wins (so the highest-priority rule's
//                       value sticks for any given style key).
//   - border          : composed from any/all of border-{color,width,style}
//                       from the matching rules — width/style/color each
//                       collapse to the highest-priority value that defined
//                       them.
function applyRulesToNode(node, rules) {
    if (!rules || rules.length === 0) { return; }
    node.attrs = node.attrs || {};
    var attrs = node.attrs;

    var names = [];
    var classes = [];
    var iconEntries = [];   // [{icon, priority}]
    var tooltips = [];      // one per matching rule that defined mm.flag-tooltip
    var styleMap = {};
    var borderParts = {};   // { width, style, color }

    for (var i = 0; i < rules.length; i++) {
        var r = rules[i];
        names.push(r.name);

        if (r["mm.flag-class"]) { classes.push(r["mm.flag-class"]); }

        if (r["mm.flag-icon"]) {
            iconEntries.push({ icon: r["mm.flag-icon"], priority: r.priority });
        }
        if (r["mm.flag-tooltip"]) { tooltips.push(r["mm.flag-tooltip"]); }

        if (r["mm.flag-text-color"])     { styleMap["mx:text-color"]      = r["mm.flag-text-color"]; }
        if (r["mm.flag-bg-color"])       { styleMap["core:color"]         = r["mm.flag-bg-color"]; }
        if (r["mm.flag-font-weight"])    { styleMap["mx:font-weight"]     = r["mm.flag-font-weight"]; }
        if (r["mm.flag-font-style"])     { styleMap["mx:font-style"]      = r["mm.flag-font-style"]; }
        if (r["mm.flag-text-transform"]) { styleMap["mx:text-transform"]  = r["mm.flag-text-transform"]; }
        if (r["mm.flag-opacity"] !== "" && r["mm.flag-opacity"] !== undefined) {
            styleMap["mx:opacity"] = r["mm.flag-opacity"];
        }
        if (r["mm.flag-font-size-scale"]) { styleMap["mx:font-size-scale"] = r["mm.flag-font-size-scale"]; }

        if (r["mm.flag-border-width"]) { borderParts.width = r["mm.flag-border-width"]; }
        if (r["mm.flag-border-style"]) { borderParts.style = r["mm.flag-border-style"]; }
        if (r["mm.flag-border-color"]) { borderParts.color = r["mm.flag-border-color"]; }
    }

    // mx:flags — additive in case the node already carries some (defensive).
    var existingFlags = String(attrs["mx:flags"] || "").split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
    var combinedFlags = existingFlags.slice();
    for (var fi = 0; fi < names.length; fi++) {
        if (combinedFlags.indexOf(names[fi]) < 0) { combinedFlags.push(names[fi]); }
    }
    if (combinedFlags.length > 0) {
        attrs["mx:flags"] = combinedFlags.join(" ");
        for (var fj = 0; fj < names.length; fj++) {
            attrs["mx:flag-" + names[fj]] = true;
        }
    }

    if (classes.length > 0) {
        var existingClasses = String(attrs["mx:flag-classes"] || "").split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
        var combinedClasses = existingClasses.slice();
        for (var ci = 0; ci < classes.length; ci++) {
            if (combinedClasses.indexOf(classes[ci]) < 0) { combinedClasses.push(classes[ci]); }
        }
        attrs["mx:flag-classes"] = combinedClasses.join(" ");
    }

    if (tooltips.length > 0) {
        // Ascending priority order (== rule iteration order). Joined with
        // newline so the browser renders one tooltip line per active flag.
        var existingTip = String(attrs["mx:flag-tooltip"] || "");
        var existingLines = existingTip ? existingTip.split("\n") : [];
        var combined = existingLines.slice();
        for (var ti = 0; ti < tooltips.length; ti++) {
            if (combined.indexOf(tooltips[ti]) < 0) { combined.push(tooltips[ti]); }
        }
        attrs["mx:flag-tooltip"] = combined.join("\n");
    }

    if (iconEntries.length > 0) {
        // Descending priority. Stable on ties so equal-priority icons preserve
        // the order they were declared (loader gives us ascending priority,
        // ties broken by source-title — predictable).
        iconEntries.sort(function (a, b) { return b.priority - a.priority; });
        var existingIcons = String(attrs["mx:icons"] || "").split("|").filter(Boolean);
        var newIcons = iconEntries.map(function (e) { return e.icon; });
        attrs["mx:icons"] = existingIcons.concat(newIcons).join("|");
    }

    for (var key in styleMap) {
        attrs[key] = styleMap[key];
    }

    if (borderParts.width || borderParts.style || borderParts.color) {
        var existing = parseBorderComposite(attrs["mx:border"]);
        var w = borderParts.width || existing.width || "1px";
        var st = borderParts.style || existing.style || "solid";
        var cc = borderParts.color || existing.color || "#888";
        attrs["mx:border"] = w + " " + st + " " + cc;
    }
}

// Run each rule's filter against the universe of titled-node titles. Returns
// { ruleName → Set<title> }. Empty `titles` → all rules map to empty sets
// without any filter calls.
function evaluateRules(rules, titles, wiki) {
    var matched = Object.create(null);
    var hasFilter = wiki && typeof wiki.filterTiddlers === "function" &&
                    typeof wiki.makeTiddlerIterator === "function";
    for (var i = 0; i < rules.length; i++) {
        var rule = rules[i];
        var set = Object.create(null);
        if (hasFilter && titles.length > 0) {
            try {
                var source = wiki.makeTiddlerIterator(titles);
                var out = wiki.filterTiddlers(rule.filter, null, source) || [];
                for (var k = 0; k < out.length; k++) { set[out[k]] = true; }
            } catch (e) {
                console.error("[mindmap-flags] rule '" + rule.name + "' filter failed", e);
            }
        }
        matched[rule.name] = set;
    }
    return matched;
}

// Bottom-up walk that stamps synthetic ancestors based on per-rule
// aggregation. Memoised: each node's leaf-count and per-rule matched-count
// are computed once. Recursion depth capped at 64 against malformed input.
function aggregateUpwards(root, rules, matchedByRule) {
    var aggregating = [];
    for (var i = 0; i < rules.length; i++) {
        if (rules[i].aggregate === "any" || rules[i].aggregate === "all") {
            aggregating.push(rules[i]);
        }
    }
    if (aggregating.length === 0) { return; }

    var MAX_DEPTH = 64;
    var warned = false;

    // Returns { totalLeaves, perRule } for the subtree rooted at `node`.
    function visit(node, depth) {
        if (depth > MAX_DEPTH) {
            if (!warned) {
                console.warn("[mindmap-flags] aggregation recursion depth exceeded — tree too deep, capping");
                warned = true;
            }
            return { totalLeaves: 0, perRule: zeroPerRule() };
        }
        var attrs = node.attrs || {};
        var directTitle = attrs["core:tiddler"];
        var total = 0;
        var perRule = zeroPerRule();

        if (directTitle) {
            total = 1;
            for (var r = 0; r < aggregating.length; r++) {
                var name = aggregating[r].name;
                if (matchedByRule[name] && matchedByRule[name][directTitle]) {
                    perRule[name] = 1;
                }
            }
        }

        var children = node.children || [];
        for (var c = 0; c < children.length; c++) {
            var sub = visit(children[c], depth + 1);
            total += sub.totalLeaves;
            for (var rn = 0; rn < aggregating.length; rn++) {
                var key = aggregating[rn].name;
                perRule[key] += sub.perRule[key];
            }
        }

        if (attrs["core:synthetic"] === true && total > 0) {
            var matching = [];
            for (var ai = 0; ai < aggregating.length; ai++) {
                var rule = aggregating[ai];
                var m = perRule[rule.name];
                if (rule.aggregate === "any" && m > 0) {
                    matching.push(rule);
                } else if (rule.aggregate === "all" && m === total) {
                    matching.push(rule);
                }
            }
            if (matching.length > 0) {
                applyRulesToNode(node, matching);
            }
        }

        return { totalLeaves: total, perRule: perRule };
    }

    function zeroPerRule() {
        var z = {};
        for (var i = 0; i < aggregating.length; i++) { z[aggregating[i].name] = 0; }
        return z;
    }

    visit(root, 0);
}

/*
 * decorateFlags(mdom, rules, wiki) → mdom
 *
 * Mutates `mdom` in place. Returns the same MDOM for chaining convenience.
 * No-ops cleanly when rules or mdom are empty / missing.
 *
 * The caller is responsible for keeping `mdom` ahead of `composer.compose` —
 * decoration runs BEFORE compose so live overlay setAttr ops can still
 * override flag-stamped values (a user "mute" gesture, for example).
 */
exports.decorateFlags = function (mdom, rules, wiki) {
    if (!mdom || !mdom.root || !rules || rules.length === 0) { return mdom; }

    var collected = collectTitledNodes(mdom.root);
    var titles = Object.keys(collected.byTitle);

    var matchedByRule = evaluateRules(rules, titles, wiki);

    // Stamp direct matches on every titled node.
    for (var ti = 0; ti < collected.allTitled.length; ti++) {
        var pair = collected.allTitled[ti];
        var matching = [];
        for (var ri = 0; ri < rules.length; ri++) {
            var rule = rules[ri];
            var set = matchedByRule[rule.name];
            if (set && set[pair.title]) { matching.push(rule); }
        }
        if (matching.length > 0) {
            applyRulesToNode(pair.node, matching);
        }
    }

    // Aggregation pass (skipped automatically if no aggregating rules exist).
    aggregateUpwards(mdom.root, rules, matchedByRule);

    return mdom;
};

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Test-only exports.

exports._applyRulesToNode = applyRulesToNode;
exports._evaluateRules = evaluateRules;
exports._collectTitledNodes = collectTitledNodes;
exports._parseBorderComposite = parseBorderComposite;

title: $:/plugins/rimir/mindmap/lib/grouped-tree.js
type: application/javascript
module-type: library

Pure-JS helpers for the grouped-tree producer. Group a flat list of items by
a key function; recursively apply an ordered list of axes to produce a nested
group/leaf structure. Exposed for unit-testing without a wiki instance.

\*/

"use strict";

var UNSET_KEY = "__unset__";

// Group `items` by the value returned from `keyFn(item)`. Preserves the order
// in which keys first appear. Items whose key is null/undefined/empty land in
// a single bucket keyed UNSET_KEY (caller decides how to label it).
function groupBy(items, keyFn) {
    var groups = [];
    var byKey = Object.create(null);
    for (var i = 0; i < items.length; i++) {
        var raw = keyFn(items[i]);
        var key = (raw === null || raw === undefined || raw === "") ? UNSET_KEY : raw;
        if (!byKey[key]) {
            byKey[key] = { key: key, items: [] };
            groups.push(byKey[key]);
        }
        byKey[key].items.push(items[i]);
    }
    return groups;
}

// Sort group entries per the axis's `sort` mode. Mutates and returns the
// array. Modes:
//   "first-seen" (default) — no-op; preserves groupBy() insertion order
//   "asc" / "desc"         — alpha (localeCompare) ascending / descending
//   "enum"                 — by position in axis.sortKeys; keys not listed
//                            sort after the enum, alpha-ascending
function sortGroups(entries, axis) {
    var mode = axis && axis.sort;
    if (!mode || mode === "first-seen") { return entries; }
    if (mode === "asc") {
        entries.sort(function (a, b) { return a.key.localeCompare(b.key); });
        return entries;
    }
    if (mode === "desc") {
        entries.sort(function (a, b) { return b.key.localeCompare(a.key); });
        return entries;
    }
    if (mode === "enum") {
        var order = Object.create(null);
        var keys = axis.sortKeys || [];
        for (var i = 0; i < keys.length; i++) { order[keys[i]] = i; }
        entries.sort(function (a, b) {
            var ai = (a.key in order) ? order[a.key] : Infinity;
            var bi = (b.key in order) ? order[b.key] : Infinity;
            if (ai !== bi) { return ai - bi; }
            return a.key.localeCompare(b.key);
        });
        return entries;
    }
    return entries;
}

// Recursively partition `leaves` through `axes`. Each axis:
//   { id, keyFn(leaf), labelFn(key), leafFilter?(leaf), sort?, sortKeys? }
// Returns an array of entries; each entry is either:
//   { kind: "leaf", leaf: <value> }
// or
//   { kind: "group", axisId, key, label, items, children }
// where `children` is the recursive result one axis deeper.
//
// When `axes` is empty, every leaf becomes a {kind:"leaf"} entry directly —
// callers get a flat list, which is the natural identity for "no grouping".
//
// Empty-branch pruning: a group whose recursive `children` ends up empty is
// dropped from the result — keeps the tree free of placeholder parents when
// downstream axis leaf-filters narrow the population to zero (e.g. a "notes"
// rrt-type bucket under a chain whose deeper axis is meetings/tasks-only).
function applyChain(leaves, axes) {
    function build(items, depth) {
        if (depth >= axes.length) {
            var out = [];
            for (var i = 0; i < items.length; i++) {
                out.push({ kind: "leaf", leaf: items[i] });
            }
            return out;
        }
        var axis = axes[depth];
        var filtered = items;
        if (typeof axis.leafFilter === "function") {
            filtered = [];
            for (var j = 0; j < items.length; j++) {
                if (axis.leafFilter(items[j])) { filtered.push(items[j]); }
            }
        }
        var groups = groupBy(filtered, axis.keyFn);
        var entries = [];
        for (var k = 0; k < groups.length; k++) {
            var g = groups[k];
            var children = build(g.items, depth + 1);
            if (children.length === 0) { continue; }
            var label = (typeof axis.labelFn === "function")
                ? axis.labelFn(g.key)
                : g.key;
            entries.push({
                kind: "group",
                axisId: axis.id,
                key: g.key,
                label: label,
                items: g.items,
                children: children
            });
        }
        return sortGroups(entries, axis);
    }
    return build(leaves, 0);
}

exports.UNSET_KEY = UNSET_KEY;
exports.groupBy = groupBy;
exports.applyChain = applyChain;
exports.sortGroups = sortGroups;
